knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Factor RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-level RLT inequalities generated solely from finite variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For bounded variables \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\) and \(l_j\le x_j\le u_j\), multiply pairs of nonnegative bound factors and introduce \(X_{ij}\) for \(x_ix_j\). Linearization gives \[X_{ij}\ge l_ix_j+l_jx_i-l_il_j,\qquad X_{ij}\ge u_ix_j+u_jx_i-u_iu_j,\] \[X_{ij}\le u_ix_j+l_jx_i-u_il_j,\qquad X_{ij}\le l_ix_j+u_jx_i-l_iu_j.\] Every point satisfying \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\) and the bounds satisfies these inequalities, so dropping the bilinear identity while retaining them produces a valid linear outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Products of nonnegative lower- and upper-bound factors yield the four linear McCormick–RLT inequalities for each lifted bilinear term.
assumptions_latex: \(l_i<u_i\) and \(l_j<u_j\) are finite.
\(X_{ij}\) represents the lifted product \(x_ix_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(x_i,x_j,X_{ij}):X_{ij}=x_ix_j\}\) over the box is contained in the displayed RLT polyhedron.

notation.meaning: lifted variable representing the product of two variables

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bound-factor RLT equals the standard bilinear box-envelope inequalities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four displayed inequalities are the standard bound-factor McCormick–RLT system, but the record lacks an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Constraint-Product RLT
children.top_down_role: RLT strengthening derived from products involving constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Product RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity rule for RLT inequalities produced by multiplying constraints by sign-known factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k(x)\ge0\) be valid on a feasible region \(F\), and let \(h(x)\ge0\) on \(F\), where \(h\) may be a variable-bound factor such as \(x_i-l_i\) or \(u_i-x_i\). Then \(g_k(x)h(x)\ge0\) is valid on \(F\). Expanding this product and replacing every monomial \(x^\alpha\) by a lifted variable \(X_\alpha\) produces a linear RLT inequality. Any consistent lift \(X_\alpha=x^\alpha\) of a point in \(F\) satisfies that inequality; therefore it remains a valid strengthening when monomial equalities are relaxed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying a valid inequality by a factor known to be nonnegative yields another valid inequality, whose lifted linearization strengthens an RLT relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(g_k(x)\ge0\) and \(h(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in F\).
All monomials in \(g_kh\) have corresponding lifted variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_k(x)h(x)\ge0\) yields a linear inequality valid for every consistent lifted point over \(F\).

notation.meaning: lifted representative of monomial x to the multi-index alpha

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonnegative constraint products are the defining validity mechanism of constraint-product RLT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sign-product validity rule is sound, but the monomial expansion and linearization require polynomial or explicitly monomial-representable functions, which is not stated. An authoritative RLT source is also required to settle the intended scope.

children.title: Integrality-Enhanced RLT

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Enhanced RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact binary–continuous product relations added to an RLT lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\in\{0,1\}\), \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\), and introduce \(W_i=yx_i\). The binary identity \(y^2=y\) and products of the bounds with \(y\) and \(1-y\) give \[l_i y\le W_i\le u_i y,\qquad l_i(1-y)\le x_i-W_i\le u_i(1-y).\] These inequalities describe the convex hull of \(W_i=yx_i\) over \(y\in\{0,1\}\) and the bounded interval for \(x_i\). Adding them and linearized identities derived from integral variables strengthens an RLT system without excluding any integer-feasible lifted point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary identities and bound products give an exact convex-hull formulation for each bounded binary–continuous product and strengthen the surrounding RLT relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\) with finite bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities equal \(\operatorname{conv}\{(y,x_i,W_i):W_i=yx_i\}\) over the stated domain.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard convex hull of a bounded binary–continuous product

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed binary–continuous product formulation is the standard exact convex hull under finite bounds, but no inspectable source supports either the hull claim or its RLT interpretation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Procedure for generating a disjunctive cut for a nonconvex MINLP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded procedure using branch-specific bound reduction, linear relaxations, and a cut-generating linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a problem \(\mathbf P\), a linear relaxation \(\mathbf{LP}=(A,a,\ell,u)\) with optimal solution \(x^\star\), and the disjunction \(x_i\leq\beta\;\vee\;x_i\geq\beta\), form \(\mathbf P'\) by imposing \(x_i\leq\beta\) and \(\mathbf P''\) by imposing \(x_i\geq\beta\). Apply bound reduction to obtain \([\ell',u']\) and \([\ell'',u'']\); generate linear relaxations \(\mathbf{SLP}'\), defined by \((A',a')\), and \(\mathbf{SLP}''\), defined by \((A'',a'')\); construct and solve CGLP (4.1); and return \((\alpha,\alpha_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given the problem, its LP relaxation and an optimal LP solution, and the stated two-term variable disjunction, create the two restricted subproblems. Reduce their bounds, generate a linear relaxation for each, solve the specified cut-generating linear program, and return the cut coefficients.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf{LP}=(A,a,\ell,u)\text{ is a linear relaxation of }\mathbf P
x^\star\text{ is an optimal solution of }\mathbf{LP}
x_i\leq\beta\;\vee\;x_i\geq\beta\text{ is the supplied disjunction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure returns the cut coefficients }(\alpha,\alpha_0).

children.title: Integer-Disjunction Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convexification across integer-induced alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Disjunction Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended convex-hull formulation for finitely many bounded polyhedral alternatives induced by integer assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the integer alternatives define nonempty bounded polyhedra \(P_k=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_kx\le b_k\}\), for \(k=1,\ldots,m\). Then \[\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{k=1}^m P_k\right)=\left\{x:\begin{array}{l}x=\sum_{k=1}^m x^k,\quad \sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_k=1,\quad \lambda_k\ge0,\\ A_kx^k\le b_k\lambda_k\quad(k=1,\ldots,m)\end{array}\right\}.\] Thus disaggregating the continuous variables by integer alternative and relaxing the alternative indicators to the simplex gives an exact extended formulation of the disjunctive convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregate variables by integer alternative, scale each bounded polyhedron by a simplex weight, and sum the copies to obtain the exact disjunctive convex hull.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_k\) is a nonempty bounded polyhedron.
The disjunction contains finitely many alternatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection of the displayed extended formulation onto \(x\) is \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_kP_k)\).

notation.meaning: polyhedron associated with integer alternative k
disaggregated variable contribution from alternative k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard bounded-polyhedral disjunctive hull formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-polyhedral disjunctive formulation is standard, but the auxiliary variables on the right-hand side are only implicitly existentially quantified. A cited authoritative formulation is needed before fixing the exact statement.

children.title: Domain-Disjunction Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convexification across partitions of continuous domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Disjunction Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull formulation for a finite partition of a bounded continuous domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\bigcup_{k=1}^m D_k\), where every \(D_k\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex. Define \(\lambda D_k=\{\lambda z:z\in D_k\}\) for \(\lambda>0\) and \(0D_k=\{0\}\). Then \[\operatorname{conv}(D)=\left\{x:x=\sum_{k=1}^m x^k,\quad x^k\in\lambda_kD_k,\quad \lambda_k\ge0,\quad \sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_k=1\right\}.\] Applying this construction to lifted graphs or epigraphs over the partition cells produces a domain-disjunctive convex relaxation; finer partitions can strengthen it by retaining more local structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite union of compact convex domain cells is convexified exactly by simplex-weighted, disaggregated copies of those cells.
assumptions_latex: \(D_k\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex for each \(k\).
The partition has finitely many cells.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed disaggregated set equals \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_kD_k)\).

notation.meaning: convex cell of the domain partition

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite convex-union hull via disaggregation and simplex weights

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simplex-weighted disaggregation formula is plausible and appropriately scoped to finite compact convex cells, but the exact hull equality and partition-strengthening claim have no cited source.

children.title: Perspective Convexification

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex-hull formulation for a bounded on–off epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(C\subset\operatorname{dom}f\) be compact and convex. For the on–off set \(S=\{(0,0,t):t\ge0\}\cup\{(1,x,t):x\in C,\ t\ge f(x)\}\), its closed convex hull is \[\left\{(z,x,t):0\le z\le1,\ x\in zC,\ t\ge \widetilde f(x,z)\right\},\] where \(\widetilde f(x,z)=zf(x/z)\) for \(z>0\), while \(x\in0C\) forces \(x=0\) and \(\widetilde f(0,0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling a convex cost by its activation variable produces the exact closed convex hull of a bounded on–off epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(C\subset\operatorname{dom}f\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}(S)=\{(z,x,t):0\le z\le1,\ x\in zC,\ t\ge\widetilde f(x,z)\}\).

notation.meaning: closed perspective on the bounded activated domain
domain scaled by the activation variable

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard perspective hull of a bounded on–off convex epigraph

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded on–off perspective formulation is mathematically plausible and fits the representation container, but its exact closed-convex-hull claim requires an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: On–Off Nonlinear Structure

knowledge_statements.title: On–Off Nonlinear Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunctive structure linking a binary activation variable to nonlinear variables and cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An on–off nonlinear epigraph is a set of the form \[S=\{(z,x,t):z=0,\ x=0,\ t\ge0\}\ \cup\ \{(z,x,t):z=1,\ x\in C,\ t\ge f(x)\},\] where \(z\in\{0,1\}\) activates the continuous vector \(x\), \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the active domain, and \(f:C\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the active nonlinear cost. Equivalently, the binary value selects between an inactive singleton in the \(x\)-space and the nonlinear active epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An on–off nonlinear set forces its continuous variables to zero when inactive and imposes a nonlinear epigraph over an active domain when switched on.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the active domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in \(S\) is exactly the stated inactive-or-active disjunction.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical on–off nonlinear epigraph definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent and matches the on–off nonlinear structure container, but no inspectable citation is provided for the adopted canonical convention, including the inactive epigraph ray.

children.title: Perspective Closure Limits
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes where perspective strengthening is incomplete or unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Closure Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession behavior at zero activation, where the positive-activation perspective formula alone is incomplete.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex function \(f\), the closed perspective is \[\widetilde f(x,z)=\begin{cases}zf(x/z),&z>0,\\ f^\infty(x),&z=0,\\ +\infty,&z<0,\end{cases}\] where \(f^\infty\) is the recession function. Hence the formula \(zf(x/z)\) restricted to \(z>0\) does not specify the closure at zero activation. If the active domain is unbounded, nonzero recession directions may survive at \(z=0\). For example, when \(f(x)=0\) on \(\mathbb R\), points \((z,x,t)=(1/k,1,0)\) belong to the perspective epigraph and converge to \((0,1,0)\), which is absent if zero activation is forced naively to \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero activation, the closed perspective is governed by the recession function; unbounded active domains can introduce nonzero limiting directions omitted by a naive formula.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The active domain may be unbounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(z=0\), closure requires \(\widetilde f(x,0)=f^\infty(x)\), not merely the assignment \(x=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: closed-perspective extension at zero uses the recession function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recession-function extension and counterexample correctly express the zero-activation closure phenomenon, but this nontrivial failure-boundary statement lacks an authoritative citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Supporting Hyperplane Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient cuts supporting a convex epigraph at a reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex on a convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). For \(\bar x\in C\) and any subgradient \(g\in\partial f(\bar x)\), the affine function \(x\mapsto f(\bar x)+g^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\) supports \(f\): \[f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+g^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\qquad(x\in C).\] Therefore \(t\ge f(\bar x)+g^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\) is valid for the epigraph \(t\ge f(x)\). Likewise, for the convex constraint \(f(x)\le0\), the inequality \(f(\bar x)+g^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\le0\) is a valid outer-relaxation cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient of a convex function defines an affine global underestimator, yielding valid cuts for convex epigraphs and convex sublevel constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex.
\(f\) is convex on \(C\), with \(g\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+g^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\) for every \(x\in C\).

notation.meaning: subdifferential of f at the reference point

children.title: Tangent Outer Approximations
children.top_down_role: Tangent-based estimators used in nonlinear outer approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent Outer Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite outer approximation formed from tangents to differentiable convex constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in C:f_j(x)\le0,\ j=1,\ldots,r\}\), where \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex and each \(f_j\) is convex and differentiable on \(C\). For finite reference sets \(Y_j\subset C\), define \[P(Y)=\left\{x\in C:f_j(y)+\nabla f_j(y)^{\mathsf T}(x-y)\le0\ \text{for every }y\in Y_j,\ j=1,\ldots,r\right\}.\] Convexity implies \(F\subseteq P(Y)\). Adding reference points only intersects \(P(Y)\) with further valid tangent halfspaces, so the resulting outer approximations are nested and nonexpanding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting finitely many tangent halfspaces of differentiable convex constraints gives an outer approximation that tightens monotonically as more tangents are added.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex.
Each \(f_j\) is convex and differentiable on \(C\).
Each \(Y_j\subset C\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq P(Y)\), and \(Y_j\subseteq Y'_j\) for all \(j\) implies \(P(Y')\subseteq P(Y)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tangent outer approximation follows from the convex first-order inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite tangent outer approximation and nesting property are correct under the stated convexity and differentiability assumptions, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Curvature Validity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Curvature conditions determining global validity of supporting or tangent estimators.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Validity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature and inequality orientations under which first-order affine cuts are globally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a differentiability point \(\bar x\), the tangent \(L_{\bar x}(x)=f(\bar x)+\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\) is a global underestimator when \(f\) is convex and a global overestimator when \(f\) is concave. Accordingly, \(L_{\bar x}(x)\le0\) is valid for a convex sublevel constraint \(f(x)\le0\), while \(L_{\bar x}(x)\ge0\) is valid for a concave superlevel constraint \(f(x)\ge0\). Reversing either curvature–orientation pairing is not generally valid; for example, tangents to a convex function need not preserve its superlevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangent cuts are globally valid for convex sublevel constraints and concave superlevel constraints; reversing these curvature–orientation pairings can remove feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\).
The stated convexity or concavity holds on the entire relaxation domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convexity validates \(f\le0\Rightarrow L_{\bar x}\le0\); concavity validates \(f\ge0\Rightarrow L_{\bar x}\ge0\).

notation.meaning: first-order affine tangent at the reference point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: global tangent under- and overestimation determined by curvature

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The curvature–orientation pairings and their failure boundary are mathematically standard and fit the condition container, but the global validity claim lacks an authoritative citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Secant Estimators
children.top_down_role: Endpoint-based linear estimators over bounded domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Secant Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Univariate secants used as global estimators on a bounded interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:[\ell,u]\to\mathbb R\), where \(\ell<u\), and define the secant \(s(x)=f(\ell)+\frac{f(u)-f(\ell)}{u-\ell}(x-\ell)\). If \(f\) is convex on \([\ell,u]\), then \(f(x)\le s(x)\) for every \(x\in[\ell,u]\), so \(s\) is a valid affine overestimator. If \(f\) is concave, the inequality reverses and \(s\) is a valid affine underestimator. In either case, equality holds at both endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The line through a univariate function’s endpoint values overestimates a convex function and underestimates a concave function throughout the interval.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell<u\)
\(f\) is finite and convex or concave on \([\ell,u]\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\le s\) in the convex case, while \(f\ge s\) in the concave case.

notation.meaning: Affine secant through the endpoint values of the function.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The secant inequalities are mathematically standard, precise, and appropriate to the leaf, but no inspectable source or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Chord Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine vertex interpolation over a simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nondegenerate simplex. Every \(x\in T\) has barycentric coordinates \(\lambda_i\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i=1\) and \(x=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i v_i\). Define the chord interpolant \(c_T(x)=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i f(v_i)\). If \(f:T\to\mathbb R\) is convex, then \(f(x)\le c_T(x)\) on \(T\); if \(f\) is concave, then \(f(x)\ge c_T(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine interpolation of vertex values over a simplex bounds a convex function from above and a concave function from below.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a nondegenerate simplex
\(f\) is finite and convex or concave on \(T\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_T\) is an affine global estimator on \(T\) with direction determined by the curvature of \(f\).

notation.meaning: Affine chord interpolant over the simplex.
Barycentric coordinates of a point in the simplex.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simplex interpolation claim and estimator directions are correct, but the record has no source with a specific locator.

children.title: Interval Width Effects
children.top_down_role: Estimator strength as determined by the current domain width.

knowledge_statements.title: Interval Width Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic tightening of one-dimensional secant estimators under bounded curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^2([\ell,u])\) be convex, let \(s\) be its endpoint secant, and suppose \(0\le f''(x)\le M\) for every \(x\in[\ell,u]\). Then the secant relaxation error satisfies \[0\le s(x)-f(x)\le \frac{M}{2}(x-\ell)(u-x)\le \frac{M}{8}(u-\ell)^2.\] Consequently, reducing the interval width from \(w\) to \(\rho w\), with \(0<\rho<1\), reduces this worst-case error bound by the factor \(\rho^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With uniformly bounded second derivative, the maximum secant gap is at most one eighth of the curvature bound times the squared interval width.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^2([\ell,u])\) is convex
\(0\le f''\le M\) on \([\ell,u]\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{x\in[\ell,u]}(s(x)-f(x))\le M(u-\ell)^2/8\).

notation.meaning: Uniform upper bound on the second derivative.

children.title: Excluded-Region Cut Family
children.top_down_role: Cuts derived from excluded nonlinear regions or explicit disjunctions.

children.title: Intersection Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts derived from intersections with excluded nonlinear regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balas-type intersection cut from a simplicial cone and a convex excluded region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{\bar x+\sum_{j=1}^k r^j\lambda_j:\lambda\ge0\}\), and let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex with \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}C\). Suppose every feasible point belongs to \(P\setminus\operatorname{int}C\). For each ray define \(\alpha_j=\sup\{t\ge0:\bar x+t r^j\in C\}\). With \(1/\infty=0\), every feasible point satisfies \[\sum_{j=1}^k\frac{\lambda_j}{\alpha_j}\ge1.\] Thus the displayed inequality separates \(\bar x\) while remaining valid for the feasible portion of the cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ray exit distances from a convex forbidden region produce a linear inequality excluding the cone apex but retaining every feasible point outside the region.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is closed and convex with \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}C\)
feasible points in the cone avoid \(\operatorname{int}C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_j\lambda_j/\alpha_j\ge1\) is a valid intersection cut.

notation.meaning: Generating rays of the polyhedral cone.
Exit distance of ray j from the excluded convex set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Balas-type formula is plausible, but its ray-exit and infinite-ray conventions require authoritative source verification before the stated version is reliable.

children.title: Disjunctive Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts derived from explicit alternative feasible regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity criterion for linear cuts derived from a finite disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{t=1}^q P_t\), where each \(P_t\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a polyhedron representing one term of a valid finite disjunction. If \(a^\top x\ge\beta\) is valid for every \(P_t\), equivalently if \(\inf\{a^\top x:x\in P_t\}\ge\beta\) for every \(t\), then it is valid for \(\bigcup_{t=1}^qP_t\) and hence for \(F\). If this valid inequality is violated by a point of an ambient relaxation containing \(F\), it is a disjunctive cut separating that relaxation point from \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality valid for every term of a valid finite disjunction is valid for their union and for the feasible set; when it excludes an ambient relaxation point, it is a disjunctive cut.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{t=1}^qP_t\)
\(a^\top x\ge\beta\) is valid on every \(P_t\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^\top x\ge\beta\) is valid for \(F\), and it is a cut when it is violated by a point of the ambient relaxation.

children.title: Excluded-Region Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric structures supporting intersection-based separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Excluded-Region Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex forbidden regions supporting globally valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), an excluded region is a set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(F\cap\operatorname{int}C=\varnothing\). If \(C\) is closed and convex and a relaxation point \(\bar x\) lies in \(\operatorname{int}C\), then \(C\) is a convex excluded region for \(\bar x\). Its boundary records where rays originating at \(\bar x\) first leave the infeasible region, and these exit points may define inequalities valid for \(F\) but violated by \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex excluded region contains no feasible point in its interior and contains the relaxation point to be separated.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\)
\(C\) is closed and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is excluded for \(F\) exactly when \(F\cap\operatorname{int}C=\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The excluded-region definition fits the geometry leaf, but no authoritative source and locator supports the terminology or associated ray-boundary interpretation.

children.title: Difference-of-Convex Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower-bounding families based on DC representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Difference-of-Convex Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex lower bounds obtained by majorizing the subtracted convex component of a DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and let \(f=g-h\) on \(X\), where \(g\) and \(h\) are convex. If \(u_h:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex or affine and satisfies \(u_h(x)\ge h(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), then \(\underline f(x)=g(x)-u_h(x)\le f(x)\) on \(X\). When \(u_h\) is affine, \(\underline f\) is convex, and \(\inf_{x\in X}\underline f(x)\) is a valid lower bound on \(\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex lower estimator for a DC function results by replacing its subtracted convex component with a valid affine upper estimator.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is convex
\(f=g-h\) with convex \(g,h\)
\(u_h\ge h\) on \(X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_X(g-u_h)\le\inf_X f\), and \(g-u_h\) is convex when \(u_h\) is affine.

notation.meaning: Global upper estimator of the subtracted convex component.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Difference of Convex (D.C.) Functions p. 58; 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

children.title: Interval-Arithmetic Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Interval-based range and lower-bound calculations.

knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Arithmetic Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range-enclosure lower bounds on a bounded box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) and let \(F(X)=[\underline F(X),\overline F(X)]\) be an inclusion interval extension of \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), meaning \(f(x)\in F(X)\) for every \(x\in X\). Then \(\underline F(X)\le\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), so the lower endpoint is a rigorous node lower bound. If interval extensions \(G_j(X)\) of constraints satisfy \(\underline G_j(X)>0\) for some requirement \(g_j(x)\le0\), the entire box is infeasible and may be discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower endpoint of an inclusion interval is a certified objective lower bound; interval constraint exclusion can also certify that a box is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a bounded box
\(F\) and \(G_j\) are inclusion interval extensions
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline F(X)\le\inf_X f\), and \(\underline G_j(X)>0\) certifies infeasibility for \(g_j\le0\).

notation.meaning: Interval enclosure of the objective range on the box.
Interval enclosure of constraint j on the box.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interval-enclosure lower bound and constraint-exclusion test are precise, but no inspectable source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Lagrangian-Dual Bound Family
children.top_down_role: Globally valid bounds derived through dualization or relaxation duals.

children.title: Lagrangian Bounds
children.top_down_role: Global lower bounds obtained from Lagrangian relaxation interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality lower bounds for minimization, including nonconvex and mixed-integer domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g_i(x)\le0,\ h_j(x)=0\}\), where \(X\) may include integrality restrictions. For multipliers \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and unrestricted \(
u_j\), define \[q(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in X}\left(f(x)+\sum_i\lambda_i g_i(x)+\sum_j
u_j h_j(x)ight).\] Every such multiplier pair yields \(q(\lambda,
u)\le p^*\). Hence \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0,
u}q(\lambda,
u)\) is a valid global lower bound, whether or not the primal problem is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing the Lagrangian over the original variable domain gives a lower bound for every sign-feasible multiplier, even for nonconvex or mixed-integer problems.
assumptions_latex: the primal problem is a minimization problem
\(\lambda\ge0\) for constraints written as \(g_i\le0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\lambda,\nu)\le d^*\le p^*\).

source_refs.locator: 6. Duality in Global Optimization p. 167

source_witnesses.locator: 6. Duality in Global Optimization p. 167

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition of a MINLP bound obtained by evaluating the decomposed Lagrangian dual function at a multiplier computed from a specified linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The MINLP bound associated with $\widehat\mu$ is defined by
\[
\underline v_{\mathrm{MINLP}}:=D(\widehat\mu)=c_0+\widehat\mu^{T}b+\sum_{k=1}^{p}\min_{y\in G_k}L_k(y;\widehat\mu),
\]
where $G_k$ is the feasible set of the $k$th Lagrangian subproblem. The multiplier $\widehat\mu$ is computed by solving the referenced linear relaxation because maximizing $D$ is generally too difficult.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The MINLP bound at mu-hat is defined as the dual-function value equal to the constant term plus the multiplier paired with b plus the sum of the minimum component Lagrangians over their respective subproblem feasible sets. Here each G_k is the feasible set of the kth Lagrangian subproblem. The multiplier is computed from a referenced linear relaxation because directly maximizing the dual function is generally too difficult.
assumptions_latex: G_k\text{ is the feasible set of the }k\text{th Lagrangian subproblem to the MINLP}\quad(k=1,\ldots,p)
\widehat\mu\text{ is computed from the referenced linear relaxation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \underline v_{\mathrm{MINLP}}=D(\widehat\mu)=c_0+\widehat\mu^Tb+\sum_{k=1}^{p}\min_{y\in G_k}L_k(y;\widehat\mu).

children.title: Relaxation-Dual Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds inherited from dual systems associated with valid relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Dual Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual bounds obtained from a convex relaxation of a nonconvex MINLP node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R\) be respectively the feasible set of a minimization problem and a convex relaxation, with objective \(f\). Let \(r^*=\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\), and let \(d_R^*\) be the optimum of any valid dual of the relaxation. Weak duality and set inclusion give \[d_R^*\le r^*\le p^*:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\] If the relaxation is convex and satisfies a constraint qualification ensuring strong duality, then \(d_R^*=r^*\); otherwise the computable dual value remains valid but may be weaker than the relaxation optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual value for a convex relaxation is a lower bound on both the relaxation and original minimization problem; strong duality can make it exact for the relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\)
the relaxation dual satisfies weak duality
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_R^*\le r^*\le p^*\), with \(d_R^*=r^*\) under strong duality.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the primal relaxation.
Optimal dual value of the relaxation.

children.title: Duality-Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes where dual bounds remain separated from primal values.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions distinguishing zero-gap convex relaxations from potentially positive-gap nonconvex formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with primal value \(p^*\) and Lagrangian-dual value \(d^*\), weak duality always gives \(d^*\le p^*\). If the continuous formulation is convex, its inequality functions are convex, its equality functions are affine, and Slater’s condition holds with finite \(p^*\), then \(d^*=p^*\). Once convexity, the constraint qualification, or continuity of the relevant value function is lost—as commonly occurs with integrality or nonconvex constraints—weak duality persists but equality need not: the gap \(p^*-d^*\) may be strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slater-regular convex problems have zero Lagrangian duality gap, while nonconvexity, integrality, or failed regularity can leave a positive gap despite weak duality.
assumptions_latex: the primal and dual values are well-defined
Slater’s condition is invoked only for the stated convex regime
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*=p^*\) in the Slater-regular convex regime; outside it, only \(d^*\le p^*\) is guaranteed.

children.title: Polynomial Bound Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Connections from polynomial MINLP structure to global lower-bounding systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Bound Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface from a polynomial MINLP node to certified polynomial lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m;\ h_j(x)=0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\), where the objective \(p\), constraints, and any polynomial encodings of discrete variables are real polynomials. A polynomial-bound interface accepts this description and returns \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) together with a certificate that \(p(x)-\gamma\ge0\) on \(K\). The certified inequality implies \[\gamma\le p^*:=\inf_{x\in K}p(x),\] so \(\gamma\) is a valid global node lower bound regardless of the certificate family used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial bounding oracle receives a semialgebraic formulation and returns a certified scalar lower bound by proving objective minus bound is nonnegative on the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(p,g_i,h_j\) are real polynomials
the returned certificate establishes nonnegativity on \(K\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p-\gamma\ge0\) on \(K\) implies \(\gamma\le\inf_{x\in K}p(x)\).

notation.meaning: Basic semialgebraic feasible set, including polynomial discrete-variable encodings when present.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate-to-lower-bound implication is correct and appropriately interface-neutral, but the record supplies no source or locator for the polynomial-bound interface.

children.title: Sum-of-Squares Bound Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Connections to sum-of-squares lower-bounding systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Sum-of-Squares Bound Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-module SOS interface for polynomial lower bounds on a continuous relaxation of a MINLP node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d\in\mathbb N\), define \[\gamma_d=\sup\left\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j,\ \sigma_j\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_0)\le 2d,\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le 2d\right\}.\] Every feasible certificate satisfies \(f(x)-\gamma\ge0\) for all \(x\in K\), so \(\gamma_d\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\). At fixed order, representing the SOS polynomials by positive-semidefinite Gram matrices yields a semidefinite-programming interface to the node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-truncated SOS decomposition of the objective minus a scalar produces a semidefinite-representable lower bound valid throughout the polynomial feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) is nonempty and \(f,g_j\in\mathbb R[x]\).
The order \(d\) satisfies \(2d\ge\max\{\deg f,\deg g_1,\ldots,\deg g_m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_d\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\).

children.title: Moment-Relaxation Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions governing access to moment-based bound families.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Relaxation Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal moment formulation compatible with the order-matched quadratic-module SOS dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\) and let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2d}\) be a real truncated moment vector. The compatible order-\(d\) moment relaxation is \[\inf_y\left\{L_y(f):y_0=1,\ M_d(y)\succeq0,\ M_{d-d_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\ \text{for }j=1,\ldots,m\right\}.\] Its conic dual is the order-\(d\) SOS bound interface with the same degree truncations. Weak duality gives \(\gamma_d\le L_y(f)\) for every moment-feasible \(y\), and equality of the two optimal values holds whenever the resulting primal-dual semidefinite pair satisfies a conic strong-duality qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching moment and localizing matrix orders gives the semidefinite primal corresponding to the order-truncated SOS lower-bound dual, with equal optimal values under conic strong duality.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), with \(f,g_j\in\mathbb R[x]\).
The order \(d\) satisfies \(d\ge d_j\) for every \(j\) and \(2d\ge\deg f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak duality gives \(\gamma_d\le\inf_y L_y(f)\); equality holds under an applicable conic strong-duality qualification.

notation.meaning: Linear functional induced by the truncated moment vector.
Order-matched localizing matrix for constraint polynomial g_j.

children.title: Adaptive Relaxation Refinement
children.top_down_role: Strengthening driven by domain partitions or observed relaxation error.

children.title: Piecewise-Linear Refinement
children.top_down_role: Adaptive subdivision for linear outer approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Linear Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive refinement of valid univariate piecewise-linear outer approximations within a global relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(P=\{\ell,u\}\) and construct a valid linear outer relaxation \(R(P)\). Select an interval \(I=[a,b]\) with nonzero relaxation error, choose \(s\in(a,b)\), and set \(P'=P\cup\{s\}\). Generate valid child-interval inequalities on \([a,s]\) and \([s,b]\), retain the parent relaxation, and define the refined formulation by intersecting the parent relaxation with a valid piecewise or disjunctive outer formulation for the children. Retain all unaffected inequalities. Stop when the prescribed error or node-processing limit is met. This construction preserves graph feasibility and ensures \(R(P')\subseteq R(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split an interval with a weak linear outer approximation, add a valid child-interval formulation while retaining the parent relaxation, and thereby preserve the nonlinear graph in a nested tighter relaxation.
assumptions_latex: A factorable univariate term \(w=\phi(x)\) is considered on a bounded interval \([\ell,u]\).
Each parent and child formulation is a valid outer relaxation of the graph or epigraph relation required by the current model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(P')\subseteq R(P)\), and every point satisfying \(w=\phi(x)\) remains feasible in \(R(P')\).

notation.meaning: Current ordered partition of the variable interval.
Linear outer relaxation induced by a partition.

children.title: Selective Expression Refinement
children.top_down_role: Refinement targeted at expressions responsible for weak bounds.

assumptions_latex: The current relaxation \(R\) contains the feasible set and has relaxable expressions indexed by \(E\).
For each \(e\in E\), a computable weakness score and a validity-preserving refinement operator are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq R'\subseteq R\), where \(F\) is the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Score-driven refinement limited to nonlinear expressions materially weakening the current lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve or inspect \(R\), compute \(s_e\ge0\) for every \(e\in E\) from a specified indicator such as envelope gap, violation, or bound sensitivity, and choose \(S\subseteq E\) by a fixed threshold or budget rule. For each \(e\in S\), apply a refinement that adds valid inequalities or partitions its argument domain; leave expressions outside \(S\) unchanged. Rebuild and resolve the relaxation, stopping when \(S=\varnothing\), the lower-bound improvement is below tolerance, or the refinement budget is exhausted. Every accepted update must yield an outer relaxation \(R'\) satisfying \(F\subseteq R'\subseteq R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank nonlinear expressions by measured relaxation weakness, refine only selected expressions, and require every update to preserve validity and tighten the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Selective Expression Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source supports the scoring, selection, and validity-preserving update specification.

children.title: Multivariate Partition Refinement
children.top_down_role: Coordinated partitions for coupled nonlinear variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Multivariate Partition Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinated box subdivision for a nonlinear term depending on several coupled variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal P=\{B\}\) and construct a valid outer relaxation \(R(\mathcal P)\). Select \(Q\in\mathcal P\) and a nonempty coordinate set \(J'\subseteq J\); split \(Q\) at interior points in the coordinates of \(J'\), producing children whose union is \(Q\). Generate a valid coupled piecewise, disjunctive, or convex-hull outer formulation from the child-box relaxations, retain the parent relaxation, and define \(R(\mathcal P')\) as its intersection with that child formulation. Stop at the prescribed gap or partition budget. The resulting refinement preserves the graph and satisfies \(G_B\subseteq R(\mathcal P')\subseteq R(\mathcal P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subdivide selected coordinates of a coupled box and intersect the retained parent relaxation with a valid joint child-box formulation, producing a nested outer approximation.
assumptions_latex: A coupled term \(w=\phi(x_J)\) has bounded box domain \(B=\prod_{j\in J}[\ell_j,u_j]\).
A valid outer relaxation can be generated on every subbox and combined into a valid formulation for their union.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_B\subseteq R(\mathcal P')\subseteq R(\mathcal P)\), where \(G_B\) is the graph feasible set on \(B\).

notation.meaning: Variables jointly appearing in the nonlinear term.
