children.title: Constraint-Activity Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction based on attainable constraint activity.

assumptions_latex: A constraint is represented as \(a\le h(x)\le b\) over the current box \(X\).
An inclusion-monotone interval extension \(H(X)=[\underline h,overline h]\) encloses \(h(X)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The propagated activity is \(H(X)\cap[a,b]\); an empty intersection certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Interval extension of the constraint expression.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward propagation from variable domains to the attainable interval of a constrained expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(A_h=H(X)\cap[a,b]\). If \(A_h=\varnothing\), declare the node infeasible. Otherwise replace the admissible activity of \(h\) by \(A_h\), and pass this interval to inverse contractors for the arguments of \(h\). For a one-sided constraint, use \([a,+\infty)\) or \(( -\infty,b]\) as appropriate. Recompute the activity after any argument-domain contraction. Because \(h(X)\subseteq H(X)\), this update cannot remove any point in \(X\) satisfying \(a\le h(x)\le b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect an interval enclosure of each constraint expression with its allowed activity range; emptiness proves infeasibility and a smaller intersection drives reverse contraction.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Activity Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward activity-propagation algorithm fits the terminal container and is plausible, but no inspectable source is supplied for the interval and inverse-contractor specification.

children.title: Interval Domain Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction based on interval enclosures of nonlinear expressions.

assumptions_latex: Each constraint has an interval inclusion function and sound inverse contractors on a bounded box \(X\).
All integer-variable contractions are intersected with their discrete domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(X'\) contains every feasible point in \(X\), and \(X'=\varnothing\) certifies box infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Current Cartesian product of variable intervals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound interval contraction of continuous and integer domains under all current constraints.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(X^{0}=X\). At sweep \(k\), apply every contractor and set \(X^{k,i}=X^{k,i-1}\cap C_i(X^{k,i-1})\), rounding any integer coordinate inward to its admissible discrete values. If an interval becomes empty, return \(X'=\varnothing\). Otherwise repeat sweeps until no endpoint changes beyond tolerance or a sweep limit is reached, and return the last box \(X'\). Soundness requires that every feasible \(x\in X^{k,i-1}\) also belongs to \(C_i(X^{k,i-1})\); consequently no feasible point is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly apply sound constraint contractors, intersect their results with current variable domains, and round integer bounds inward until reaching a fixed point or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Interval Domain Propagation

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Propagation Interaction
children.top_down_role: Mutual strengthening between activity-based and interval-based contraction.

assumptions_latex: Forward activity maps and reverse domain contractors are sound and inclusion-monotone.
All updates are intersections with current intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iterate contains the feasible set, the interval sequence is nested, and any common fixed point is propagation-stable.

notation.meaning: Vector of variable and expression intervals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point interaction between expression activities and variable-domain contractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) perform one complete forward activity sweep followed by all reverse domain contractions, with every result intersected into \(D\). Soundness gives \(F(D)\subseteq F(T(D))\) as represented feasible assignments, while contraction gives \(T(D)\subseteq D\) componentwise. Thus the iteration \(D^{k+1}=T(D^k)\) is nested and never removes a feasible assignment. If \(D^{k+1}=D^k\), then \(D^k\) is propagation-stable for the chosen operators. Applying one propagation family can enable strict contractions by another, so sweeps continue until a common fixed point or a prescribed limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward activity tightening and reverse domain contraction reinforce one another; repeated sound intersections form a nested sequence that preserves all feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interaction property fits the leaf, but no source is supplied and the use of F(D) makes the preservation inclusion ambiguous; for actual feasible assignments, sound contraction normally preserves the same feasible set while shrinking its interval representation.

children.title: Expression-Graph Domain Propagation
children.top_down_role: Forward and reverse propagation through lifted expressions.

assumptions_latex: The factorable constraint system is represented by an acyclic expression graph with bounded leaf domains.
Every elementary operation has a sound interval extension and a sound inverse contractor on its domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned leaf box contains every feasible assignment represented by the initial box; an empty node interval certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Interval attached to graph node v.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-backward interval propagation on an acyclic lifted expression graph.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Algorithms Based on Interval Methods p. 46

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each leaf its current domain. In topological order, update every internal node by \(I_v\leftarrow I_v\cap\phi_v^{I}((I_u)_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(v)})\), then intersect root intervals with their constraint ranges. In reverse topological order, apply a sound inverse contractor for \(\phi_v\) to contract each child interval using \(I_v\) and the other child intervals. Iterate forward and reverse sweeps until stable or limited; return the contracted leaf domains. If any \(I_v=\varnothing\), return infeasible. All intersections and inverse updates must retain every graph-consistent feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate intervals forward through a lifted expression graph, intersect constrained roots, then propagate backward with inverse contractors until stable or infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Graph Domain Propagation

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Algorithms Based on Interval Methods p. 46

children.title: Fixed-Integer Feasibility Tightening
children.top_down_role: Continuous-domain contraction conditional on a discrete assignment.

assumptions_latex: Integer variables are fixed to an assignment \(z=\bar z\) admissible in the current discrete domain.
A sound continuous feasibility contractor is available for the resulting nonlinear system over box \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X'=\varnothing\) excludes \(\bar z\); otherwise every feasible \((x,\bar z)\) with \(x\in X\) satisfies \(x\in X'\).

notation.meaning: Contracted continuous box conditional on the assignment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous contraction and assignment exclusion conditional on fixed integer values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Substitute \(z=\bar z\) into every constraint and initialize \(X^0=X\). Apply sound feasibility contractors for the reduced continuous system, optionally including expression-graph propagation, until an empty interval, a fixed point, or a work limit occurs. If an interval becomes empty, declare \(\bar z\) infeasible and add a valid exclusion of that complete assignment. Otherwise return the contracted box \(X'\subseteq X\) for processing under \(\bar z\). The contraction is conditional: bounds in \(X'\) may be imposed globally only when separately justified for every remaining integer assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix an integer assignment, contract the remaining continuous domains using the reduced constraints, and exclude the assignment if contraction proves infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Integer Feasibility Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional contraction and complete-assignment exclusion procedure fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the stated algorithm and validity boundary.

children.title: Probing-Based Domain Reduction
children.top_down_role: Conditional propagation under tentative integer or bound decisions.

assumptions_latex: A tentative decision \(D\) and its complementary branch \(\bar D\) cover the current domain.
Propagation under either decision is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An infeasible probe deletes its decision; bounds valid in both surviving probes may be imposed before branching.

notation.meaning: Domain obtained by propagation under D.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporary branching decisions used to infer unconditional exclusions or common bound contractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select \(D\), save the current domain \(X\), impose \(D\), and propagate to obtain \(X_D\) or infeasibility. Restore \(X\), impose \(\bar D\), and propagate to obtain \(X_{\bar D}\) or infeasibility. If \(X_D=\varnothing\), permanently impose \(\bar D\); if \(X_{\bar D}=\varnothing\), permanently impose \(D\); if both are empty, declare the node infeasible. If both survive, replace \(X\) only by bounds valid for their union, for example \(X\cap\operatorname{hull}(X_D\cup X_{\bar D})\). Stop after the chosen probe or work budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporarily test complementary decisions, propagate each case, discard infeasible decisions, and retain only bound reductions valid across all surviving cases.
knowledge_statements.title: Probing-Based Domain Reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complementary-probing algorithm and interval-hull update are plausible and appropriately scoped, but the record has no authoritative source locator.

children.title: Optimization-Based Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction obtained through auxiliary optimization over valid relaxations.

children.title: Full-Space OBBT
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary bound optimization over the complete current relaxation.

assumptions_latex: The current full-space relaxation \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\) is a valid outer approximation and includes incumbent cutoff \(f\le U\) when available.
The auxiliary optimization problems are solved with certified bounds adequate for the requested tightening.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \([\ell_i,u_i]\) by \([\max\{\ell_i,L_i\},\min\{u_i,U_i\}]\) preserves every point in \(R\).

notation.meaning: Current full-space relaxation in original and lifted variables.
Certified lower bound on the minimum of coordinate i.
Certified upper bound on the maximum of coordinate i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-based tightening using the complete current lifted relaxation and cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each selected coordinate \(i\), solve the two auxiliary relaxation problems \[m_i=\inf\{x_i:(x,w)\in R\},\qquad M_i=\sup\{x_i:(x,w)\in R\}.\] Obtain certified bounds \(L_i\le m_i\) and \(U_i\ge M_i\), then update \(\ell_i\leftarrow\max\{\ell_i,L_i\}\) and \(u_i\leftarrow\min\{u_i,U_i\}\). If an updated lower bound exceeds its upper bound, declare the node infeasible. Rebuild \(R\) after material changes and repeat according to the scheduling rule. Output the contracted box together with the auxiliary-solver certificates used for every accepted endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize and maximize selected variables over the complete current relaxation, then use certified auxiliary bounds to contract their domains without removing relaxation-feasible points.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space OBBT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The full-space OBBT algorithm uses the correct certified-bound directions and fits the terminal container, but no inspectable source supports the formulation or certificate requirements.

children.title: Localized Node-Specific OBBT Family
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary tightening restricted to selected nodes, variables, or nonlinear neighborhoods.

children.title: Localized OBBT
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary tightening restricted to selected nonlinear neighborhoods.

assumptions_latex: The current search node has relaxation region \(R_N\subseteq [\ell^N,u^N]\).
A valid incumbent cutoff \(U\) is available, and every node-feasible improving point belongs to \(R_N\cap\{x:f(x)\le U\}\).
The localization region \(L_N\) contains every point whose retention is required for the node subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\ell^{\mathrm{loc}}_j=\inf\{x_j:x\in R_N\cap L_N,\ f(x)\le U\},\qquad u^{\mathrm{loc}}_j=\sup\{x_j:x\in R_N\cap L_N,\ f(x)\le U\}.\] Replacing \([\ell^N_j,u^N_j]\) by \([\ell^{\mathrm{loc}}_j,u^{\mathrm{loc}}_j]\) is valid for the retained node subproblem. If either auxiliary problem is solved only by a valid bound, the lower endpoint uses a valid lower bound on the infimum and the upper endpoint a valid upper bound on the supremum. Empty localized feasibility certifies infeasibility of the retained subproblem, not necessarily of the original model.

notation.meaning: Relaxation and localization regions at node N.
Current variable-bound vectors at node N.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact localized OBBT for a minimization node; localization validity is explicitly conditional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a variable index \(j\), form the localized cutoff relaxation \(S_N^{\mathrm{loc}}=R_N\cap L_N\cap\{x:f(x)\le U\}\). Solve one minimization and one maximization of \(x_j\) over \(S_N^{\mathrm{loc}}\), then intersect the resulting interval with the current node interval. The localization is globally safe at node \(N\) only when it contains every node-feasible point that can improve the incumbent; otherwise the contraction applies solely to the explicitly retained localized subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Localized OBBT optimizes each selected variable over a cutoff relaxation restricted to a neighborhood, with validity limited to points guaranteed to remain in that neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.title: Localized OBBT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf and the conditional validity language is mathematically cautious, but no citation supports this particular localized OBBT construction or its infeasibility interpretation.

children.title: Node-Specific OBBT
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary tightening performed within a selected search-node domain.

assumptions_latex: The branch-and-bound node \(N\) supplies valid bounds \(\ell^N\le x\le u^N\).
The relaxation \(R_N\) contains every feasible point assigned to node \(N\).
For minimization, \(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every processed variable \(j\), define \(S_N=R_N\cap\{x:f(x)\le U\}\) and compute \(\alpha_j=\inf_{x\in S_N}x_j\) and \(\beta_j=\sup_{x\in S_N}x_j\). Then the valid node update is \[\ell^N_j\leftarrow\max\{\ell^N_j,\alpha_j\},\qquad u^N_j\leftarrow\min\{u^N_j,\beta_j\}.\] Valid outward bounds on \(\alpha_j\) and \(\beta_j\) may replace exact optima. If \(S_N=\varnothing\) is certified, node \(N\) is infeasible or cannot improve the incumbent.

notation.meaning: Valid relaxation at branch-and-bound node N.
Current lower and upper variable bounds at node N.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-local OBBT using the current node relaxation and incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each selected variable \(x_j\), optimize \(x_j\) in both directions over the current node relaxation augmented by the incumbent cutoff. Initialize with the node bounds, replace each endpoint only by a certified valid bound from its auxiliary problem, repeat if desired after propagation, and return either the contracted node box or an infeasibility certificate. Because \(R_N\) is node-specific, the resulting bounds need not be valid outside node \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node-specific OBBT tightens selected bounds by minimizing and maximizing each variable over the current node relaxation with the incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Specific OBBT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and node-local cutoff formulation fit the container, but the record has no source for the auxiliary-bound and pruning claims.

children.title: Neighborhood Selection
children.top_down_role: Policies identifying local structures worth auxiliary optimization.

assumptions_latex: A valid node relaxation \(R_N\) and cutoff \(U\) define \(S_N=R_N\cap\{x:f(x)\le U\}\).
A candidate neighborhood \(L_N(\rho)\) is indexed by a size parameter \(\rho\).
The required retained set \(T_N\subseteq S_N\) is specified by the search policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A neighborhood is admissible for exact contraction of \(T_N\) precisely when \(T_N\subseteq L_N(\rho)\). A selection rule may choose \[\rho_N\in\arg\min_{\rho}\{C_N(\rho):T_N\subseteq L_N(\rho)\},\] where \(C_N(\rho)\) estimates auxiliary-solve cost. OBBT over \(S_N\cap L_N(\rho_N)\) then gives valid bounds for \(T_N\). If containment is unverified, the selected neighborhood defines a heuristic restriction and cannot justify pruning any point of \(S_N\setminus L_N(\rho_N)\).

notation.meaning: Set that the localized procedure must retain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition and cost-aware selection rule for localized OBBT neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Neighborhood selection chooses the restriction used by localized OBBT. The mathematical validity requirement is containment of every point to which the resulting bounds will be applied. Subject to that requirement, the neighborhood may be selected by predicted solve cost, distance from a relaxation solution, branching depth, or bound width. Smaller neighborhoods can strengthen or accelerate auxiliary problems, but they do not preserve node-wide validity unless the required containment is certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a low-cost neighborhood that contains every point to which the tightened bounds will apply; otherwise the contraction is only heuristic.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits neighborhood admissibility, but the asserted precise containment criterion and cost-minimizing policy are policy-specific and uncited. The necessity direction also requires clarification because bounds can remain valid accidentally without full set containment.

children.title: Dual-Information OBBT Family
children.top_down_role: Bound tightening using dual information or dual surrogates.

children.title: Lagrangian OBBT
children.top_down_role: Bound tightening informed by Lagrangian relaxation values.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation is \(S=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), with \(X\) simple enough for valid infimum bounds.
Multipliers satisfy \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m_+\).
All auxiliary infimum bounds are globally valid over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each variable \(j\), define \[q_j^-(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\left(x_j+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(x)\right),\qquad q_j^+(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\left(-x_j+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(x)\right).\] Weak duality gives \(q_j^-(\lambda)\le\inf_{x\in S}x_j\) and \(-q_j^+(\lambda)\ge\sup_{x\in S}x_j\). Hence \(x_j\ge q_j^-(\lambda)\) and \(x_j\le-q_j^+(\lambda)\) are valid relaxation bounds; optimizing or improving \(\lambda\) can strengthen them.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian lower bounds for the two variable directions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality form of Lagrangian variable-bound tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Lagrangian OBBT replaces each exact variable-extremization subproblem by a dual lower bound. For the lower endpoint it dualizes the relaxation constraints in the minimization of \(x_j\); for the upper endpoint it dualizes them in the minimization of \(-x_j\). Any dual-feasible nonnegative multipliers yield outward-valid endpoints, while stronger dual bounds yield tighter intervals. No strong-duality assumption is required for validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lagrangian OBBT derives outward-valid variable bounds from weak-duality bounds on minimizing each variable and its negative.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian OBBT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality kind fits the leaf and the weak-duality signs are internally consistent, but no inspectable citation supports this formulation as Lagrangian OBBT.

children.title: Dual-Surrogate OBBT
children.top_down_role: Bound tightening driven by approximate or inherited dual information.

assumptions_latex: The valid relaxation is \(S=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\).
The aggregation vector satisfies \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m_+\).
The surrogate auxiliary problems are solved exactly or with outward-valid bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(x\in S\) satisfies the surrogate inequality \(\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(x)\le0\), so \[S\subseteq S_\lambda:=\left\{x\in X:\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(x)\le0\right\}.\] Consequently, \[\inf_{x\in S_\lambda}x_j\le\inf_{x\in S}x_j,\qquad \sup_{x\in S_\lambda}x_j\ge\sup_{x\in S}x_j.\] The surrogate extrema therefore define valid, possibly weaker, bounds for \(x_j\). Multiple surrogate inequalities may be retained provided each uses nonnegative multipliers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-aggregation surrogate for variable-bound auxiliary problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dual-surrogate OBBT replaces some or all relaxation constraints by nonnegative weighted aggregates. It minimizes and maximizes selected variables over the resulting surrogate relaxation, then intersects the outward-valid extrema with the current box. Because nonnegative aggregation preserves every point satisfying the original inequalities, the surrogate bounds are valid. Their strength depends on the chosen multipliers and on how many independently valid aggregates are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-surrogate OBBT optimizes variables over nonnegative aggregations of relaxation constraints, producing valid but potentially weaker bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Surrogate OBBT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nonnegative aggregation gives the stated outer relaxation, but the record lacks a source connecting this construction to dual-surrogate OBBT. The representation kind is plausible but should be checked against an algorithm or method characterization in the source.

children.title: Multiplier Quality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Tightening effectiveness under differing multiplier reliability.

assumptions_latex: The auxiliary minimization problem has dual function \(q(\lambda)\) and primal optimum \(p^*\).
The stated dual-feasible set is \(D\).
Variable tightening uses dual lower bounds, so larger values of \(q\) are stronger.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Multiplier quality separates into three regimes. If \(\lambda\in D\), then \(q(\lambda)\le p^*\), giving a valid outward bound; its loss is the dual gap \(p^*-q(\lambda)\). If \(\lambda^*\in\arg\max_{\lambda\in D}q(\lambda)\) and strong duality holds, then \(q(\lambda^*)=p^*\), recovering the relaxation endpoint. If \(\lambda\notin D\), weak duality is unavailable and the resulting endpoint is not certified. Thus approximate multipliers affect strength, whereas dual infeasibility affects validity.

notation.meaning: Primal optimum of an OBBT auxiliary problem.
An optimal dual multiplier when one exists.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and strength regimes for multipliers used in dual-information OBBT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an OBBT auxiliary minimization, dual-feasible multipliers always produce valid lower bounds by weak duality. Among such multipliers, bound quality is ordered by the dual-function value. Dual-optimal multipliers recover the primal relaxation value only when strong duality and attainment hold. Inexact but dual-feasible multipliers preserve validity, while multipliers violating sign or other dual-feasibility conditions provide no general bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-feasible multipliers preserve validity; better dual values strengthen tightening, and optimal multipliers are exact only under strong duality.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Quality Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the leaf and the distinction between dual feasibility, bound strength, and exactness is mathematically standard, but no specific authoritative source is supplied.

children.title: OBBT Scheduling-Selection Policy
children.top_down_role: Policies selecting variables, nodes, and frequencies for auxiliary tightening.

children.title: OBBT Scheduling Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies governing when auxiliary tightening is invoked.

assumptions_latex: At search state \(k\), the solver has node data \(D_k\), eligible variables \(J_k\), and remaining OBBT budget \(B_k\).
Each scheduled auxiliary solve returns an outward-valid bound or a certified infeasibility result.
The policy never applies a bound outside the relaxation region used to derive it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A scheduling policy is a map \(\pi(D_k,B_k)=(A_k,M_k)\), where \(A_k\subseteq J_k\times\{-,+\}\) selects variable directions and \(M_k\) specifies their execution order and permitted iterations. Execute the selected auxiliary problems until \(A_k\) is exhausted, \(B_k\) is spent, infeasibility is certified, or no accepted improvement exceeds tolerance \(\tau\). Intersect all returned intervals with the current box. Scheduling changes computational effort and attainable contraction, but validity follows from the individual auxiliary certificates rather than from \(\pi\).

notation.meaning: Search-state information and remaining OBBT budget.
Scheduled variable-direction pairs and execution metadata.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract budgeted scheduling interface for valid OBBT auxiliary solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the eligible set, computational budget, improvement tolerance, and node trigger. At each trigger, use current relaxation information to select variable-direction auxiliary problems, order or parallelize them, solve within the budget, apply certified contractions, and optionally reschedule after material bound changes. Terminate on budget exhaustion, lack of accepted improvement, node pruning, or completion of the selected set. Root-only, periodic, event-driven, and adaptive schedules are instances of this policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An OBBT schedule chooses when, in what order, and within what budget valid variable-bound subproblems are solved.
knowledge_statements.title: OBBT Scheduling Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the scheduling leaf, but the policy map, stopping rules, and listed schedule classes are an uncited synthesized framework rather than a source-supported OBBT scheduling policy.

children.title: OBBT Variable Selection
children.top_down_role: Policies choosing variables for auxiliary bound optimization.

assumptions_latex: The eligible variables are indexed by \(J\), with current widths \(w_j=u_j-\ell_j\).
For each direction, a score uses only available relaxation information.
Every unselected variable retains its current valid interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Let \(s_j^-\) and \(s_j^+\) estimate tightening benefit for the lower and upper directions, and let \(c_j^-,c_j^+>0\) estimate their costs. Under budget \(B\), a valid selection rule chooses \[A\subseteq J\times\{-,+\},\qquad \sum_{(j,d)\in A}c_j^d\le B,\] commonly by ranking \(s_j^d/c_j^d\) or solving the associated budgeted selection problem. OBBT is run only for \(A\); certified results are intersected with current bounds. Selection affects efficiency and strength, not validity of retained bounds.

notation.meaning: Eligible variable set and current variable width.
Estimated benefit and cost for direction d.
Selected variable-direction pairs and total budget.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted selection of variable-direction pairs for OBBT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: OBBT variable selection restricts auxiliary optimization to variable-direction pairs predicted to yield useful contraction. Initialize an eligible set, compute benefit and cost scores from widths, relaxation solutions, violations, branching relevance, or prior tightening, and choose a subset within the available budget. Solve the selected lower- and upper-bound problems and return the contracted box. Variables not selected remain unchanged and may be reconsidered after the relaxation changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable selection spends the OBBT budget on directions with favorable predicted tightening relative to auxiliary-solve cost.
knowledge_statements.title: OBBT Variable Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the selection leaf, but benefit-to-cost scoring and the budgeted selection formulation are implementation-dependent and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Frequency–Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Computational regimes balancing tightening frequency against auxiliary cost.

assumptions_latex: At decision epoch \(k\), invoking OBBT has cost \(C_k\ge0\) and produces certified box contraction.
The contraction has an estimated downstream benefit \(G_k\ge0\), measured in a common work-equivalent scale.
The estimates are conditional on current search information \(D_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For a tradeoff parameter \(\eta>0\), the one-epoch net value of invocation is \(V_k=G_k-\eta C_k\). A threshold policy invokes OBBT when \(\mathbb{E}[G_k\mid D_k]>\eta\mathbb{E}[C_k\mid D_k]\), subject to any hard budget. Increasing invocation frequency weakly increases direct OBBT expenditure, but need not reduce total search work because contractions can prevent descendant nodes or strengthen relaxations. Therefore no universally optimal fixed frequency follows without a model of \(G_k\), \(C_k\), and their state dependence.

notation.meaning: Invocation cost and estimated downstream benefit.
Conversion factor between direct cost and downstream benefit.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision-theoretic statement of OBBT invocation frequency versus computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: OBBT frequency should balance the direct cost of auxiliary solves against expected downstream savings from tighter relaxations, stronger propagation, and node elimination. A state-dependent invocation is justified when its estimated benefit exceeds its weighted cost; otherwise postponement is preferred. This principle determines a policy criterion, not a universal numerical frequency, because both benefit and cost depend on node depth, relaxation strength, incumbent quality, and prior contractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invoke OBBT when expected downstream search savings exceed weighted auxiliary-solve cost; no fixed frequency is universally optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Frequency–Cost Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the tradeoff leaf, but the expected-value threshold and work-equivalent objective are a proposed decision model with no supporting source.

children.title: Objective-Dual Domain Reduction
children.top_down_role: Domain reduction based on incumbent cutoffs and relaxation dual information.

children.title: Objective-Cutoff Propagation
children.top_down_role: Contraction induced by the current incumbent cutoff.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with feasible incumbent value \(U\).
The relaxation region \(R\) contains every feasible point under consideration.
The objective expression \(f\) or a valid relaxation of its epigraph is available for propagation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible point capable of improving the incumbent lies in \(S_U=R\cap\{x:f(x)\le U\}\). Hence the exact cutoff-induced interval for variable \(x_j\) is \[\left[\inf_{x\in S_U}x_j,\ \sup_{x\in S_U}x_j\right].\] Intersecting the current interval with any outward enclosure of this projection is valid. If \(S_U=\varnothing\) is certified, the region cannot improve the incumbent and may be pruned. A contractor may approximate these projections provided it never removes a point of \(S_U\).

notation.meaning: Relaxation restricted by the objective cutoff.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact projection characterization for minimization with a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Objective-cutoff propagation adds the necessary inequality \(f(x)\le U\) to the current relaxation, where \(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent. It then contracts variable domains using consequences of that inequality together with the relaxation constraints. The contraction is valid because every point that can strictly improve the incumbent satisfies the cutoff; certified emptiness proves that the current region cannot improve it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the incumbent objective cutoff contracts variable domains while preserving every feasible point that can improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Cutoff Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is compatible with the topic, and the projection characterization is internally coherent, but there is no citation for the cutoff-propagation and pruning claims.

children.title: Reduced-Cost Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Contraction based on valid relaxation reduced costs.

assumptions_latex: A minimization LP relaxation has optimal value \(z_L\) and a feasible incumbent cutoff \(U\ge z_L\).
Variable \(x_j\) has bounds \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\).
The reported reduced cost is dual-feasible and uses the stated minimization sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(x_j=\ell_j\) at the relaxation optimum and its reduced cost satisfies \(r_j>0\), dual feasibility gives \(f_{\mathrm{LP}}(x)\ge z_L+r_j(x_j-\ell_j)\); therefore every point with objective at most \(U\) satisfies \[x_j\le \ell_j+\frac{U-z_L}{r_j}.\] If \(x_j=u_j\) and \(r_j<0\), then \(f_{\mathrm{LP}}(x)\ge z_L+(-r_j)(u_j-x_j)\), so \[x_j\ge u_j-\frac{U-z_L}{-r_j}.\] Each result is intersected with the current interval.

notation.meaning: LP relaxation lower bound and incumbent cutoff.
Reduced cost of variable j under minimization convention.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP reduced-cost tightening for bounded variables in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dual-feasible reduced cost certifies the minimum objective degradation caused by moving a nonbasic bounded variable away from its active bound. The available objective gap \(U-z_L\) therefore limits that movement. Positive reduced cost at a lower bound yields an upper-bound contraction; negative reduced cost at an upper bound yields a lower-bound contraction. Zero reduced cost provides no contraction through this formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid LP reduced costs convert the incumbent gap into a maximum allowed movement away from a variable's active bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Bound Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind appropriately captures the reduced-cost bound formula, but its validity depends on the exact LP reduced-cost convention and dual certificate. No source is provided to verify those details.

children.title: Dual-Multiplier Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Contraction guided by valid relaxation dual multipliers.

assumptions_latex: For every point in the relaxation, a dual certificate gives \(f(x)\ge L+\sum_{i=1}^m\mu_i s_i(x)\).
The slacks satisfy \(s_i(x)\ge0\), and the multipliers satisfy \(\mu_i\ge0\).
A feasible incumbent cutoff \(U\ge L\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every relaxation point satisfying \(f(x)\le U\) obeys \[\sum_{i=1}^m\mu_i s_i(x)\le U-L.\] Consequently, whenever \(\mu_i>0\), \[s_i(x)\le\frac{U-L}{\mu_i}.\] This is a verifiable cutoff-domain certificate. If a slack is affine or monotone in a variable, the displayed upper bound propagates directly to a variable bound; otherwise any sound contractor for \(s_i(x)\le(U-L)/\mu_i\) may be used. Multipliers with \(\mu_i=0\) yield no individual contraction.

notation.meaning: Certified relaxation lower bound and incumbent cutoff.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic nonnegative-slack certificate for cutoff-based dual-multiplier contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dual-multiplier bound tightening combines a certified relaxation lower bound with the incumbent gap. When the dual certificate decomposes objective excess into nonnegative multiplier-weighted slacks, the cutoff limits each slack having a positive multiplier. Propagating those slack limits through affine or monotone constraint expressions contracts variable domains. Validity requires a genuine dual certificate; arbitrary multiplier estimates do not suffice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid dual decomposition converts the incumbent gap into upper bounds on positively weighted slacks, which can propagate to variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Multiplier Bound Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the stated construction, and the algebra follows from the assumed decomposition, but no source establishes that decomposition as the intended dual-multiplier tightening method or supports its model-specific propagation.

children.title: Bound-Reduction Closure Calculus
children.top_down_role: Repeated and coordinated application of complementary reduction operators.

children.title: Propagation Closure
children.top_down_role: Stable domains under repeated feasibility-based propagation.

assumptions_latex: The current node domain is a box \(D^0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) containing every feasible point of the node subproblem.
The propagation operator \(P\) is contracting and feasibility-valid: \(P(D)\subseteq D\), and every feasible point in \(D\) belongs to \(P(D)\).
Domain updates are performed in exact arithmetic, or outward rounding preserves validity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^\star\) is a propagation-closed, feasibility-valid reduction of \(D^0\).
review_flags: exact MINLP propagation-closure source not supplied
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines closure for repeated, feasibility-valid box contraction at one MINLP search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(D^0\), define \(D^{k+1}=P(D^k)\) for \(k\geq 0\). A domain \(D^\star\) is the propagation closure of \(D^0\) when \(D^\star=\bigcap_{k\geq 0}D^k\) and \(P(D^\star)=D^\star\). If finite-precision propagation terminates after \(K\) sweeps, its operational closure is \(D^K\) with \(P(D^K)=D^K\). Feasibility validity implies that every feasible point of the node subproblem contained in \(D^0\) remains in every \(D^k\), hence also in \(D^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation closure is the fixed domain reached by repeatedly applying valid feasibility-based contractions; it retains every feasible point from the original node domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Closure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent because fixed-point equality is imposed rather than inferred, but the exact infinite-iteration notion and terminology of propagation closure require a specific authoritative source.

children.title: Combined FBBT–OBBT Closure
children.top_down_role: Stable domains under alternating feasibility- and optimization-based tightening.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined FBBT–OBBT Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines exact and tolerance-based stability under alternating feasibility- and optimization-based bound tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D^0\) be the current node box and apply complete FBBT and OBBT sweeps alternately. An exact combined FBBT–OBBT closure is an attained domain \(D^\star\subseteq D^0\) satisfying \(F(D^\star)=D^\star\) and \(O(D^\star)=D^\star\). Under finite-precision stopping tolerances, an operational closure is instead a domain for which neither sweep improves any bound by more than its prescribed tolerance; this does not assert exact fixed-point equality. Because both sweeps are feasibility-valid contractions, every node-feasible point retained by \(D^0\) remains in every generated domain. An empty component interval certifies node infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating valid FBBT and OBBT reaches an exact combined closure when neither sweep changes the domain; tolerance-based stopping yields only an operationally stable domain.
assumptions_latex: The current node domain is a box \(D^0\).
The operators \(F\) and \(O\) are contracting and preserve every feasible point of the node subproblem.
Every OBBT bound used in the update is globally valid for its stated relaxation.
Exact closure and tolerance-based operational closure are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An exact closure is invariant under both \(F\) and \(O\); an operational closure is stable only to the prescribed tolerances, and both preserve node feasibility.

notation.meaning: Exact or operational combined closure domain, as specified.

children.title: Integer–Continuous Reduction Feedback
children.top_down_role: Coordination between discrete inference and nonlinear domain contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer–Continuous Reduction Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies bidirectional reduction feedback between discrete inference and nonlinear contraction within one MINLP node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from a joint node state \(S^0\), repeatedly apply discrete inference and nonlinear contraction, for example \(S^{k+1}=C(I(S^k))\), while communicating every domain change to the other procedure. Stop with infeasibility if any discrete domain or continuous interval becomes empty. In exact arithmetic, stop at a jointly closed state \(S^\star\) only after verifying \(I(S^\star)=S^\star\) and \(C(S^\star)=S^\star\). Under finite-precision stopping rules, return an operationally stable state when neither procedure changes a domain by more than its prescribed tolerance; exact fixed-point equality is then not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate discrete inference and nonlinear contraction, exchanging all reductions, until exact joint closure or explicitly tolerance-based stability is reached; an empty domain certifies infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Discrete inference \(I\) and nonlinear contraction \(C\) are feasibility-valid contractions on a common node state.
Every reduction produced by either procedure is communicated to the other.
The stopping rule distinguishes exact equality from tolerance-based stability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned nonempty state is either jointly closed under \(I\) and \(C\) or explicitly labeled operationally stable under the prescribed tolerances.

notation.meaning: Joint integer and continuous node state.

children.title: Node-Bounding Architectures
children.top_down_role: Architectures for generating globally valid bounds at search nodes.

children.title: Continuous Convex-Relaxation Bounding
children.top_down_role: Node bounding after relaxation of all integrality.

assumptions_latex: The node problem is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F_N\).
The continuous convex relaxation has feasible set \(R_N\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(F_N\subseteq R_N\), after all integrality restrictions are removed.
The relaxation objective \(\underline f\) underestimates the original objective \(f\) on \(F_N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N\leq\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x)\), so \(L_N\) is a valid node lower bound.

notation.meaning: Original feasible set at node N.

review_flags: locator provisionally supports convex lower bounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounding obtained by convexification and relaxation of every discrete restriction.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the continuous relaxation bound by \(L_N=\inf\{\underline f(x):x\in R_N\}\), with \(L_N=+\infty\) when \(R_N=\varnothing\). For every \(x\in F_N\), inclusion gives \(x\in R_N\) and underestimation gives \(\underline f(x)\leq f(x)\). Therefore \(L_N\leq\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x)\). If \(R_N\) is empty, then \(F_N\) is empty and the node is infeasible. If \(L_N\) is no smaller than a known incumbent value, the node cannot improve that incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing all integrality and solving a valid convex relaxation gives a lower bound for a minimization node and may certify pruning.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Convex-Relaxation Bounding

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

children.title: Mixed-Integer Convex-Relaxation Bounding
children.top_down_role: Node bounding while retaining selected or all discrete restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The node is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F_N\).
The convex relaxation retains restrictions \(x_j\in Z_j\) for indices \(j\in J_r\) and has feasible set \(M_N\) satisfying \(F_N\subseteq M_N\).
The relaxed objective \(\underline f\) underestimates the original objective on \(F_N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N^{\mathrm{MI}}\leq\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x)\), and retaining more valid discrete restrictions cannot weaken the bound.

notation.meaning: Indices whose discrete restrictions are retained.

review_flags: supplied locator supports convex lower bounding but not specifically retained integrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex node relaxation retaining a selected subset, possibly all, of the discrete domains.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(L_N^{\mathrm{MI}}=\inf\{\underline f(x):x\in M_N\}\). Since \(F_N\subseteq M_N\) and \(\underline f(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_N\), the value \(L_N^{\mathrm{MI}}\) is a valid node lower bound. If \(R_N\) denotes the corresponding relaxation with all integrality removed, then \(M_N\subseteq R_N\), so \(\inf_{x\in R_N}\underline f(x)\leq L_N^{\mathrm{MI}}\). Thus retained discrete restrictions can strengthen, but cannot invalidate, the lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex relaxation retaining selected integer domains yields a valid lower bound at least as strong as its fully continuous counterpart.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Convex-Relaxation Bounding

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

children.title: Multi-Level Node Bounding
children.top_down_role: Hierarchies of inexpensive and progressively stronger node relaxations.

assumptions_latex: For a minimization node, relaxation feasible sets satisfy \(F_N\subseteq R_N^m\subseteq\cdots\subseteq R_N^1\).
Every relaxation objective \(\underline f_k\) underestimates the original objective on \(F_N\).
Each level is solved to a certified lower bound before its pruning decision is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(L_k\) is valid; with a common objective, \(L_1\leq\cdots\leq L_m\leq\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set of relaxation level k.
Certified lower bound from level k.

review_flags: hierarchical policy itself needs a more specific source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential node bounding by nested relaxations of increasing strength and computational cost.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At level \(k=1,\ldots,m\), compute \(L_k=\inf\{\underline f_k(x):x\in R_N^k\}\). Stop and prune if \(R_N^k=\varnothing\) or \(L_k\geq U\); otherwise proceed to level \(k+1\) when the prescribed escalation rule requests a stronger bound. If all levels fail to prune, return the strongest computed bound. Every \(L_k\) is valid. When all levels use the same relaxed objective, nesting additionally yields \(L_1\leq\cdots\leq L_m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve increasingly strong valid relaxations, pruning as soon as one suffices and otherwise returning the strongest computed node bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Level Node Bounding

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The individual lower-bound facts are correct, but the cited convex-lower-bounding section does not specifically support the proposed multi-level escalation algorithm or hierarchy. A source addressing hierarchical node bounding is required.

children.title: Integer-Variable Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching driven by unresolved discrete domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Variable Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive domain partition for one unresolved integer variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an unresolved integer variable \(x_j\) with finite domain \(Z_j\subseteq\mathbb Z\), and choose an integer threshold \(t\in\mathbb Z\) satisfying \(\min Z_j\leq t<\max Z_j\). Define \(Z_j^-=\{z\in Z_j:z\leq t\}\) and \(Z_j^+=\{z\in Z_j:z\geq t+1\}\). Create two child nodes by replacing \(Z_j\) with \(Z_j^-\) and \(Z_j^+\), respectively, while inheriting all other parent restrictions. Then both child domains are nonempty, \(Z_j^-\cap Z_j^+=\varnothing\), and \(Z_j^-\cup Z_j^+=Z_j\), so every parent-feasible integer assignment belongs to exactly one child.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split an unresolved finite integer domain at an integer threshold into two nonempty, disjoint child domains whose union is the parent domain.
assumptions_latex: The selected variable \(x_j\) has a finite domain \(Z_j\subseteq\mathbb Z\) containing at least two values.
The threshold satisfies \(t\in\mathbb Z\) and \(\min Z_j\leq t<\max Z_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The child domains \(Z_j^-\) and \(Z_j^+\) form a disjoint exhaustive partition of \(Z_j\).

notation.meaning: Current finite domain of the selected integer variable.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Continuous-Variable Spatial Branching
children.top_down_role: Subdivision of continuous domains involved in nonconvex expressions.

assumptions_latex: A continuous variable \(x_j\) has current bounded interval \([\ell_j,u_j]\) with \(\ell_j<u_j\).
The split point satisfies \(s\in(\ell_j,u_j)\).
All node relaxations remain valid on the restricted child boxes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The child boxes cover the parent box, and repeated exhaustive subdivision preserves every parent-feasible point.
review_flags: source addresses continuous partition strategies generally
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial subdivision of a bounded continuous coordinate used by nonconvex relaxations.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select \(x_j\) and \(s\), then create child boxes \(D^-=D\cap\{x:x_j\leq s\}\) and \(D^+=D\cap\{x:x_j\geq s\}\). The children satisfy \(D=D^-\cup D^+\); their intersection is confined to \(x_j=s\). Rebuild or restrict each convex relaxation on its child box and process both children unless a valid pruning test removes one. Branching is exhaustive because every parent-feasible point lies in at least one child, while narrower intervals can reduce nonlinear relaxation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split a bounded continuous coordinate at an interior point, rebuild valid child relaxations, and retain exhaustive coverage of the parent domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Variable Spatial Branching

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

children.title: Expression-Oriented Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching guided by weak or violated nonlinear expression relaxations.

assumptions_latex: A factorable nonconvex expression has an auxiliary variable \(w_e\) and a valid relaxation on the current box.
A relaxation solution \((\bar x,\bar w)\) is available.
At least one variable in the expression has a nondegenerate bounded domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected split is exhaustive and targets an expression whose current relaxation is locally weak.

notation.meaning: Expression relaxation discrepancy at the relaxation solution.

review_flags: exact expression-oriented branching rule and source not supplied
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branches on variables supporting a weak nonlinear expression relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each candidate expression \(e\), compute \(\delta_e=|\bar w_e-e(\bar x)|\) or another certified relaxation-error score. Select an expression with maximal prescribed score, then choose a bounded argument \(x_j\) whose subdivision is predicted to reduce that expression's relaxation error. Split the domain of \(x_j\) exhaustively, using an integer-domain partition when \(x_j\) is discrete and an interval partition when it is continuous. Reconstruct the expression relaxation in each child and return the resulting child nodes for bounding and pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure nonlinear relaxation error, choose a weak expression and one of its arguments, then exhaustively branch to strengthen child relaxations.
knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Oriented Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed discrepancy score and argument-selection rule are plausible but are not uniquely standard, and no source supports this exact expression-oriented branching formulation.

children.title: Integer–Continuous Branching Coordination
children.top_down_role: Policies balancing discrete fractionality, bound impact, propagation, and nonlinear error.

assumptions_latex: The candidate set contains valid exhaustive branches on unresolved integer domains and bounded continuous domains.
Each candidate has nonnegative, comparably scaled estimates of bound gain, propagation gain, and nonlinear-error reduction.
A deterministic tie-breaking rule is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected branch remains exhaustive while balancing discrete and nonlinear search information.
review_flags: coordination score is a generic formalization rather than a uniquely standardized rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic score-based coordination of admissible integer and continuous branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(b\in\mathcal B\), compute normalized estimates \(G_{m bound}(b)\), \(G_{m prop}(b)\), and \(G_{m nl}(b)\), and set \(S(b)=\alpha G_{m bound}(b)+\beta G_{m prop}(b)+\gamma G_{m nl}(b)\), where \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\geq0\) and \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=1\). Integer fractionality may enter the integer candidate score or admissibility test. Select \(b^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{b\in\mathcal B}S(b)\), apply its exhaustive partition, and update gain estimates from the resulting child bounds and propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score admissible integer and continuous branches using normalized bound, propagation, and nonlinear-error gains, then apply the highest-scoring exhaustive partition.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer–Continuous Branching Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted composite score is an invented generic formalization rather than a canonical coordination policy. A source is needed to justify the selected factors, normalization, and update mechanism as field knowledge.

children.title: Incumbent Generation for Global MINLP

children.title: Integer-Assignment NLP Search
children.top_down_role: Continuous local search after selecting a discrete assignment.

assumptions_latex: A complete integer assignment \(z=\hat z\) satisfies the current discrete domains.
The resulting continuous nonlinear program is well-defined on its remaining variable bounds.
The NLP solver returns either a locally feasible point or a failure status under specified tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any returned feasible point supplies a valid incumbent value, but local NLP failure does not certify assignment infeasibility.
review_flags: exact fixed-integer NLP heuristic source not supplied
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal local search in the continuous subproblem induced by a fixed discrete assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(z=\hat z\) and solve the continuous nonlinear program \(\min_y f(y,\hat z)\) subject to \(g(y,\hat z)\leq0\), \(h(y,\hat z)=0\), and the current bounds on \(y\), using a local NLP method from one or more initial points. If the solver returns \(\hat y\) satisfying all original MINLP constraints within the feasibility tolerance, output \((\hat y,\hat z)\) and update the incumbent when its objective is better. Otherwise report heuristic failure only; without a global infeasibility certificate, the fixed assignment must not be discarded solely because local search failed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix a discrete assignment and locally solve the remaining NLP; a feasible result improves the incumbent, while solver failure proves nothing globally.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Assignment NLP Search

children.title: Rounding-Repair Primal Heuristic
children.top_down_role: Primal construction from relaxation solutions followed by nonlinear feasibility repair.

children.title: Relaxation-Based Rounding
children.top_down_role: Candidate construction from mixed-integer relaxation solutions.

assumptions_latex: A relaxation solution \((\bar y,\bar z)\) is available, with integer-variable domains \(Z_j\subseteq\mathbb Z\).
Each rounding choice belongs to the current discrete domain.
Ties and any required coupling-aware ordering are resolved by a fixed rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(\hat z\) is discrete-domain feasible, but it need not satisfy the original nonlinear or coupling constraints.

notation.meaning: Current discrete domain of integer variable j.

review_flags: exact relaxation-rounding heuristic source not supplied
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initial discrete assignment for subsequent nonlinear feasibility repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each integer index \(j\), choose \(\hat z_j\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{v\in Z_j}|v-\bar z_j|\), or apply the prescribed coupling-aware rounding order while maintaining membership in \(Z_j\). Return \(\hat z\) as the candidate discrete assignment and pass it to a repair or fixed-integer NLP phase. Componentwise rounding guarantees only \(\hat z_j\in Z_j\); it does not guarantee satisfaction of nonlinear constraints, linear coupling constraints, or logical constraints. Therefore the rounded point becomes an incumbent only after feasibility is checked against the original MINLP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round relaxation values to allowed discrete values, then require repair and an original-model feasibility check before accepting an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Based Rounding

children.title: Nonlinear Feasibility Repair
children.top_down_role: Restoration of nonlinear feasibility after discrete candidate construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Feasibility Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-integer nonlinear repair after rounding a relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a rounded integer vector \(\hat y\in Y\cap\mathbb Z^p\) and reference point \(\bar x\), solve the restoration problem \[\min_{x,s}\;\rho(x,\bar x)+\lambda\sum_{i=1}^m s_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x,\hat y)\le s_i,\;s_i\ge0,\;x\in X.\] Initialize at \(\bar x\), use a local nonlinear solver, and stop at a stationary point or a prescribed resource limit. Return \((x,\hat y)\) as a repaired incumbent only when every residual satisfies \(g_i(x,\hat y)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\); otherwise report repair failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix the rounded integers and minimize nonlinear constraint violation plus displacement. Accept the result only if all original constraints meet the feasibility tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the continuous node domain.
\(g_i:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) are evaluable for fixed \(\hat y\).
\(\rho(x,\bar x)\ge0\) and \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i g_i(x,\hat y)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) implies that \((x,\hat y)\) is a feasible incumbent candidate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and fixed-integer repair formulation fit the leaf, but no cited source supports this particular restoration objective, penalty update, or acceptance rule.

children.title: Repair Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes where rounded candidates resist nonlinear repair.

knowledge_statements.title: Repair Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural reasons a fixed-integer nonlinear repair cannot certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed rounded assignment \(\hat y\), define the infimal maximum violation by \[v_\infty(\hat y)=\inf_{x\in X}\max_{1\le i\le m}\max\{0,g_i(x,\hat y)\}.\] If \(v_\infty(\hat y)>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\), no continuous repair retaining \(\hat y\) can produce an \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\)-feasible point. Conversely, failure of a local restoration solve does not establish infeasibility: nonconvexity, an unsuitable starting point, or termination before reaching a feasible basin may prevent the solver from finding a repair even when the infimal violation is at most the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the infimal maximum constraint violation for the fixed integers exceeds the feasibility tolerance, those integers cannot be repaired. Failure of a local nonlinear solve alone is not an infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
\(m\in\mathbb N\) and \(g_i(x,\hat y)\le 0\), for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), are the original constraints under the fixed integer assignment.
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_\infty(\hat y)>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\Rightarrow\nexists x\in X:\max_{1\le i\le m}g_i(x,\hat y)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\).

notation.meaning: infimal maximum positive constraint violation for the fixed assignment

children.title: Diving Feasibility-Pump Heuristic Family
children.top_down_role: Mixed-integer primal heuristics adapted to nonlinear feasibility.

children.title: Diving Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Progressive restriction heuristics for constructing mixed-integer candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Diving Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-local diving that progressively fixes discrete variables and re-solves relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start from an active node relaxation with solution \((x^0,y^0)\) and an empty fixing set \(F_0\). At iteration \(k\), choose an unfixed integer index \(j_k\), select \(z_k\in\mathbb Z\cap[\ell_{j_k},u_{j_k}]\), set \(F_{k+1}=F_k\cup\{y_{j_k}=z_k\}\), and re-solve the resulting relaxation. Backtrack or terminate if it is infeasible. Stop when all integer variables are fixed or a resource limit is reached; submit any solution satisfying integrality and original nonlinear feasibility as an incumbent candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly fix selected integer variables, re-solve the relaxation, and optionally backtrack. A dive succeeds only when it reaches a feasible integral point.
assumptions_latex: \(y\in\mathbb Z^p\) denotes the discrete variables.
Each fixing produces a solvable relaxation or an infeasibility response.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^k\in\mathbb Z^p\) and \(g(x^k,y^k)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\mathbf1\) yield an incumbent candidate.

notation.meaning: integer fixings imposed after k diving steps
integer variable selected at step k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and iterative fixing scheme fit diving heuristics, but no source supports the MINLP-specific relaxation, backtracking, and feasibility interface.

children.title: Feasibility-Pump Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Alternating-search interfaces targeting integrality plus nonlinear feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Pump Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternation between nonlinear relaxation feasibility and projection onto discrete assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation-feasible point \(w^0=(x^0,y^0)\), alternate two operators. The discrete projection produces \(z^k=P_I(y^k)\in Y\cap\mathbb Z^p\). The nonlinear projection then computes \[w^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in R}\;d(y,z^k),\] where \(R\) is the nonlinear relaxation feasible set. Detect repeated pairs \((w^k,z^k)\) and perturb or terminate. Output \(w^k\) only when its integer coordinates are integral and it satisfies the original nonlinear constraints within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate integer projection with a nonlinear-relaxation solve that approaches the projected assignment. Handle cycles explicitly and accept only original-feasible integral points.
assumptions_latex: \(R\subseteq X\times Y\) is the node's nonlinear relaxation feasible set.
\(P_I\) maps bounded discrete coordinates to admissible integer values.
\(d\) is a nonnegative distance on discrete coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w^k\in R\) and \(y^k=z^k\in Y\cap\mathbb Z^p\) certify feasibility for the integrality requirements represented by \(P_I\).

notation.meaning: distance used by the pump projection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The alternating-projection algorithm fits the feasibility-pump interface leaf and is internally coherent, but it has no inspectable citation for the nonlinear MINLP variant.

children.title: Nonlinear Feasibility Adaptation
children.top_down_role: Adaptations required when linear primal heuristics encounter nonlinear constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Feasibility Adaptation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-pump adaptation using nonlinear restoration rather than linear projection alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After obtaining an integer target \(z^k\), compute the next continuous point by solving \[\min_{x,y,s}\;d(y,z^k)+\lambda_k\sum_{i=1}^m s_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x,y)\le s_i,\;s_i\ge0,\;(x,y)\in X\times Y.\] Increase \(\lambda_k\) when violation stagnates, perturb \(z^k\) upon cycling, and terminate at a resource limit. Accept a point only if \(y\) is integral and all original nonlinear residuals are at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adapt the pump by jointly penalizing distance to an integer target and nonlinear violations, increasing the violation penalty when progress stalls.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) define the nonlinear constraints.
\(d(y,z)\ge0\) and \(\lambda_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in\mathbb Z^p\) and \(\max_i g_i(x,y)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) make \((x,y)\) an incumbent candidate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The penalized nonlinear-restoration algorithm fits the adaptation leaf, but the particular slack formulation, penalty increase, and cycling policy require a supporting source.

children.title: Multistart Fixed-Integer Search
children.top_down_role: Multiple local continuous searches for selected discrete assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistart Fixed-Integer Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple local NLP searches over selected integer assignments and continuous starting points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose finitely many integer assignments \(y^1,\ldots,y^K\in Y\cap\mathbb Z^p\). For each \(y^k\), choose starts \(x^{k,1},\ldots,x^{k,r_k}\in X\) and run a local nonlinear solver on \[\min_{x\in X}\;f(x,y^k)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g(x,y^k)\le0.\] Retain every returned point meeting the original feasibility tolerance, and output the retained point with smallest objective value. If none is retained, report heuristic failure; do not infer global infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run local NLP solves from several starts for several fixed integer assignments, retaining the best feasible result without claiming global optimality or infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(K<\infty\) and \(r_k<\infty\).
Each \(y^k\) satisfies the discrete-domain restrictions.
The local solver returns a candidate and termination status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^*,y^*)\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x,y):(x,y)\text{ was retained}\}\) is the heuristic incumbent output.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the multistart fixed-integer-search role and appropriately avoids global claims, but no source supports this selected procedure.

children.title: Node-Selection Fathoming Calculus
children.top_down_role: Search-tree management and globally valid removal of resolved regions.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Global Optimization: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications
