children.title: Bound-Based Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Removal based on comparison of valid node bounds with the incumbent.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Based Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe pruning of a minimization node using a valid lower bound and incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_N\) be the feasible set represented by node \(N\), let \(L_N\) satisfy \(L_N\le\inf_{z\in S_N}f(z)\), and let \(U\) be the objective value of a globally feasible incumbent. For absolute optimality tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\ge0\), node \(N\) may be fathomed when \[L_N\ge U-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}.\] Indeed, no point in \(S_N\) can improve the incumbent by more than the prescribed tolerance. The rule is unsafe if \(L_N\) is merely a local objective value rather than a valid node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, prune a node when its valid lower bound cannot improve the incumbent beyond the chosen absolute optimality tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(L_N\le\inf_{z\in S_N}f(z)\).
\(U=f(\bar z)\) for a globally feasible incumbent \(\bar z\).
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N\ge U-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\Rightarrow N\) may be fathomed without losing a solution improving \(U\) by more than \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind and absolute-tolerance fathoming rule are mathematically appropriate, but the record supplies no branch-and-bound citation or locator.

children.title: Infeasibility-Based Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Removal based on valid propagation or relaxation infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility-Based Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe node removal from a valid proof that its represented domain is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A node \(N\) may be fathomed for infeasibility when a sound propagation system derives an empty variable domain, or when a relaxation \(R_N\) satisfying \(S_N\subseteq R_N\) is certified infeasible. In the relaxation case, the verifiable certificate establishes \(R_N=\varnothing\), hence \(S_N=\varnothing\). A local nonlinear solver's failure, an infeasible stationary point, or failure to find a feasible point is not by itself such a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prune a node when sound propagation empties a domain or a valid relaxation is certified infeasible. Mere failure of a local solve is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(S_N\) is the node's original feasible set.
\(R_N\) is a valid relaxation with \(S_N\subseteq R_N\).
Propagation and relaxation certificates are checked by sound rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_N=\varnothing\Rightarrow S_N=\varnothing\), so node \(N\) may be fathomed.

notation.meaning: original feasible set at node N
valid relaxation feasible set at node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the leaf, and the relaxation-set implication is correct, but the permitted certificate mechanisms and MINLP interpretation lack cited support.

children.title: Solution-Based Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Removal when a node solution resolves the relevant discrete and nonlinear gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Based Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fathoming when a node-feasible solution closes the certified node objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_N\) be the feasible set represented by minimization node \(N\), including its discrete restrictions and declared nonlinear-feasibility acceptance rules. Suppose \(L_N\) is a certified lower bound satisfying \(L_N\le\inf_{z\in S_N}f(z)\), and a node solve returns \(z_N\in S_N\). For an absolute optimization tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\ge0\), the node may be fathomed by solution when \[f(z_N)-L_N\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}.\] Then no feasible descendant of \(N\) can improve upon \(z_N\) by more than \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\), and \(z_N\) may be submitted as an incumbent candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-feasible integral solution permits solution-based fathoming when its objective is within the declared absolute tolerance of a certified node lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(S_N\) contains exactly the node points accepted as feasible under the declared discrete and nonlinear-feasibility rules.
\(L_N\le\inf_{z\in S_N}f(z)\).
\(z_N\in S_N\).
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(z_N)-L_N\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\Rightarrow f(z_N)-f(z)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\) for every \(z\in S_N\), so node \(N\) may be fathomed to that tolerance.

notation.meaning: accepted feasible set represented by node N
node-feasible solution returned by the node solve

children.title: Node-Selection Strategy Family
children.top_down_role: Node-selection families balancing bound progress and incumbent discovery.

children.title: Best-Bound Node Selection
children.top_down_role: Node selection prioritizing the strongest global bound candidate.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Bound Node Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection of the open node with the strongest global lower-bound priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, maintain a finite set \(\mathcal O\) of unfathomed open nodes, each with a valid lower bound \(L_N\). Select \[N_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{N\in\mathcal O}L_N,\] using a fixed deterministic rule to break ties. Remove \(N_k\) from \(\mathcal O\), process it, and insert any unfathomed children. If all open-node bounds are valid, then \(\min_{N\in\mathcal O}L_N\) is a valid lower bound on every feasible solution remaining in the search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the open node having the smallest valid lower bound. The minimum open-node bound remains a global bound on unexplored solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal O\) is finite and nonempty at selection.
Each \(L_N\) is a valid lower bound for node \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{N\in\mathcal O}L_N\) is selected, and \(\min_{N\in\mathcal O}L_N\) bounds all remaining feasible objectives from below.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and best-bound priority are appropriate. The global-bound statement implicitly requires the open nodes to cover all remaining unexplored feasible solutions, and the record has no supporting citation.

children.title: Depth-First Node Selection
children.top_down_role: Node selection prioritizing deeper exploration of the active search path.

knowledge_statements.title: Depth-First Node Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stack-based selection that follows the newest branch before revisiting alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain unfathomed open nodes in a last-in, first-out stack \(\mathcal S\). Push the root initially. At each iteration, pop the top node \(N_k\), process it, and push its unfathomed children in a fixed order; the last child pushed is processed next. When a node has no retained children, selection automatically backtracks to the most recently stacked alternative. Terminate when \(\mathcal S=\varnothing\) or another valid global stopping condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a last-in, first-out stack to pursue one branch deeply, automatically backtracking to the most recent unexplored alternative.
assumptions_latex: The search tree has a designated root.
Only unfathomed nodes are stored in \(\mathcal S\).
Child insertion order is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_k=\operatorname{top}(\mathcal S)\) is processed before every node pushed earlier and lying below it in the stack.

notation.meaning: last-in, first-out stack of open nodes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stack algorithm accurately represents depth-first node selection and fits the leaf, but no branch-and-bound source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Hybrid Node Selection
children.top_down_role: Policies combining bound progress with depth-oriented exploration.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Node Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit switching between LIFO depth-first and best-bound priorities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a finite nonempty collection \(\mathcal O_k\) of open nodes, valid lower bounds \(L_N\), and a LIFO ordering of those nodes. Let \(q_k\in\{\mathrm{bound},\mathrm{depth}\}\) be determined by a prescribed switching rule using search state available at iteration \(k\). Select \[N_k\in\begin{cases}\operatorname*{argmin}_{N\in\mathcal O_k}L_N,&q_k=\mathrm{bound},\\ \{\operatorname{top}(\mathcal O_k)\},&q_k=\mathrm{depth},\end{cases}\] where \(\operatorname{top}(\mathcal O_k)\) denotes the most recently inserted open node in the maintained LIFO ordering. Break best-bound ties deterministically, process \(N_k\), and update the open-node collection and its ordering. This priority choice changes search order; correctness of any fathoming or global stopping claim additionally requires valid bounds, sound fathoming rules, and the corresponding search-completeness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Switch by a prescribed rule between the smallest-bound open node and the most recently inserted open node. The switch changes search order, while global claims require valid bounds, sound fathoming, and suitable completeness conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal O_k\) is finite and nonempty at selection.
Each \(L_N\) is a valid lower bound for node \(N\).
The LIFO ordering, switching rule, and tie-breaking rule are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_k\) determines whether iteration \(k\) uses best-bound priority or LIFO depth-first priority without changing the feasible regions represented by the open nodes.

notation.meaning: open-node collection with a maintained LIFO ordering at iteration k
valid lower bound of node N
most recently inserted open node in the LIFO ordering

children.title: Incumbent–Bound Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Search regimes balancing primal discovery against global-bound improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent–Bound Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node selection may trade rapid incumbent discovery against rapid improvement of the global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, let the active nodes be \(\mathcal A\), let \(L_N\) be a valid lower bound at node \(N\), and let \(U\) be the incumbent value. Best-bound selection chooses an element of \(\arg\min_{N\in\mathcal A}L_N\), directly targeting improvement of the global bound \(L=\min_{N\in\mathcal A}L_N\). Depth-oriented selection may find feasible points and reduce \(U\) sooner. Either policy preserves bound validity, but convergence requires fairness: every node that remains eligible and cannot be fathomed must eventually be processed or have a descendant processed. A hybrid policy may prioritize a normalized combination of bound promise and depth while retaining this fairness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best-bound search strengthens the global lower bound, while depth-oriented search often improves the incumbent sooner. Hybrid selection remains convergent only if unresolved eligible regions are eventually refined.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem and every \(L_N\) is a valid node lower bound.
Nodes are fathomed only by valid infeasibility, dominance, or incumbent-bound tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every iteration, \(L\leq v^*\leq U\), and node-selection preferences do not invalidate this enclosure when fairness is retained.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for active node N
objective value of the best known feasible solution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the container, but the fairness condition and global enclosure require an authoritative node-selection source and an explicit assumption that active nodes cover every unfathomed feasible region.

children.title: Relaxation Consistency under Refinement
children.top_down_role: Consistency families connecting domain contraction with closing relaxation error.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Consistency under Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency is stated for nested mixed-integer spatial regions whose continuous widths vanish and discrete choices stabilize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\times Y\) be the closed feasible set of a minimization problem, where \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is compact and \(Y\) is finite. Let \(R_k=B_k\times Y_k\) be nonempty nested regions, let \(v(R_k)=\inf\{f(x,y):(x,y)\in F\cap R_k\}\), and let a node relaxation either certify infeasibility or return a valid finite lower bound \(L(R_k)\leq v(R_k)\). The relaxation family is consistent under refinement if, whenever \(\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0\) and \(Y_k\) is eventually constant, it satisfies both conditions: if \(F\cap R_k\neq\varnothing\) for every \(k\), then \(v(R_k)-L(R_k)\to0\); and if some \(F\cap R_k\) is empty, the relaxation eventually certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation is refinement-consistent when its lower-bound error vanishes along every feasible nested sequence with shrinking continuous boxes and stabilized finite discrete choices, and it eventually detects infeasibility along an infeasible sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is compact, \(Y\) is finite, and the feasible set \(F\) is closed.
Each finite relaxation value is a valid lower bound on its region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every qualifying feasible sequence, \(\lim_{k\to\infty}(v(R_k)-L(R_k))=0\); an infeasible qualifying sequence is eventually certified infeasible.

notation.meaning: regional optimal value of the original problem
closed feasible set of the original problem

source_refs.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

children.title: Exhaustive-Partition Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence families based on exhaustive refinement of unresolved regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive-Partition Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic convergence of deterministic spatial branch-and-bound under exhaustive refinement and consistent regional bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider branch-and-bound for minimizing a continuous objective \(f\) over a compact feasible set with finite integer projection. Suppose every node lower bound is valid, every infinite nested chain of generated regions has vanishing continuous diameter and eventually fixed integer choices, and the relaxations are consistent under refinement. Suppose node processing is fair and feasible upper-bound generation is regionally consistent: along every feasible limiting chain, generated feasible values approach its regional infimum. Let \(U_k\) be the incumbent value and let \(L_k\) be the minimum lower bound over active nodes, with \(L_k=U_k\) after the active queue is exhausted. Then \(L_k\to v^*\) and \(U_k\to v^*\). Every accumulation point of incumbent feasible points whose objective values converge to \(v^*\) is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous objective on a compact feasible set, exhaustive fair refinement with consistent regional lower and feasible upper bounds makes the global lower and incumbent bounds converge to the global optimum; limit points of convergent incumbents are optimal.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is compact, the objective \(f\) is continuous, and the integer projection is finite.
Every unresolved infinite branch is refined exhaustively and processed fairly.
Regional lower- and feasible upper-bounding mechanisms are consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}L_k=\lim_{k\to\infty}U_k=v^*\), and every accumulation point of incumbent feasible points with values converging to \(v^*\) is globally optimal.

notation.meaning: minimum valid lower bound over active nodes after iteration k, or the incumbent value after queue exhaustion
incumbent objective value after iteration k

children.title: Finite Epsilon-Termination for Global MINLP
children.top_down_role: Finite termination families for mixed discrete and spatial search with positive tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Epsilon-Termination for Global MINLP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination with a positive absolute optimality tolerance for bounded mixed-integer spatial search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varepsilon>0\). Consider spatial branch-and-bound on a compact domain with finitely many integer assignments. Assume branching reaches, after finitely many descendants, regions of arbitrarily small continuous diameter. Assume uniformly consistent bounding: there exists \(\delta>0\) such that every region \(R\) with stabilized integer choices and \(\operatorname{diam}(R)\leq\delta\) either is certified infeasible or admits valid bounds satisfying \(U(R)-L(R)\leq\varepsilon\). If node selection is fair and nodes with \(L(R)\geq U-\varepsilon\) are fathomed, then only finitely many nodes are processed before the global gap satisfies \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\). The returned incumbent is therefore \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly closing regional bounds, finite discrete choices, exhaustive finite-depth branching, and fair selection imply finite termination at any positive absolute optimality tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\), the domain is compact, and the integer projection is finite.
Bounding consistency is uniform over sufficiently small stabilized regions.
Branching and node selection satisfy finite-depth refinement and fairness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After finitely many processed nodes, \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\) and the incumbent \(\hat x\) satisfies \(f(\hat x)\leq v^*+\varepsilon\).

children.title: Exact Finiteness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Special structural regimes supporting termination without positive optimality tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Finiteness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient finite-cell regime for zero-tolerance termination of spatial branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact finite termination is guaranteed under the following finite-cell condition. The bounded mixed-integer domain admits a finite partition \(\mathcal P\) reachable by the algorithm's branching rules such that, for every cell \(R\in\mathcal P\), either infeasibility is finitely certified or the node relaxation is exact, \(L(R)=v(R)\), and an attaining feasible point is finitely recoverable whenever \(v(R)<+\infty\). If node selection is fair and branching reaches each required cell after finitely many decisions, then incumbent-bound fathoming closes every cell after finitely many operations. Consequently the algorithm terminates with zero optimality gap. Without finite reachability or exactness on terminal cells, asymptotic consistency alone does not imply exact finite termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero-tolerance finite termination follows when finitely reachable terminal cells have exact relaxations or finite infeasibility certificates; asymptotic consistency by itself is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The search domain has a finite partition reachable by the permitted branching rules.
Every terminal cell has an exact relaxation or a finite infeasibility certificate.
An optimizer of each feasible terminal cell can be recovered finitely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates after finitely many nodes with \(L=U=v^*\).

notation.meaning: true optimal value on cell R
relaxation lower bound on cell R

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-cell condition is mathematically plausible and the condition kind fits the regime container, but its zero-tolerance termination claim is nontrivial and has no cited support.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If Assumptions 13.1 and 13.2 hold and an optimality cut is added whenever the heuristic finds a local solution, then Algorithm 13.1 terminates after finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumptions 13.1 and 13.2, Algorithm 13.1 terminates finitely if every local solution found by the heuristic triggers an optimality cut.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact finiteness, a convex compact finiteness regime, and attraction regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm-specific definition and supporting concepts for the exact-finiteness analysis of Algorithm 13.1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Algorithm 13.1 is called finite when it converges after finitely many steps for \(\epsilon=0\). If problem (13.1) is a convex MINLP, its feasible set \(S\) is compact, and Algorithm 13.1 uses NLP bounds, then the algorithm is finite and implicitly enumerates all possible solutions. For a local minimizer \(x^*\), define \(\operatorname{attr}(x^*)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid\operatorname{locmin}(x)=x^*\}\), where \(\operatorname{locmin}(x)\) is the solution point returned by the local-search method initialized at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact finiteness means convergence in finitely many steps at zero tolerance. For a convex MINLP with compact feasible set, Algorithm 13.1 using NLP bounds is finite and implicitly enumerates all solutions. The attraction region of a local minimizer contains precisely the starting points from which the local search returns that minimizer.

children.title: Global Outer-Approximation Architectures

children.title: Spatial Outer Approximation
children.top_down_role: Outer approximation embedded within continuous-domain partitioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Spatial Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer approximation is localized to boxes in a spatial branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a bounded MINLP and an initial spatial box \(B_0\). For each active node box \(B\), construct convex or linear underestimators of the objective and constraint functions that are valid throughout \(B\), and solve the resulting mixed-integer outer approximation to obtain a lower bound \(L(B)\). Use feasible NLP solutions to update the incumbent \(U\). Fathom \(B\) if its relaxation is infeasible or \(L(B)\geq U-\varepsilon\); otherwise branch on an integer decision or subdivide a continuous interval, rebuild or strengthen the local estimators on each child, and continue. Stop when no active node has lower bound below \(U-\varepsilon\), returning the incumbent and the global bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spatial outer approximation repeatedly solves nodewise outer relaxations, updates feasible incumbents, and partitions domains until every remaining node is infeasible or within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every node estimator is valid on its tagged spatial box.
Node relaxation optima are valid lower bounds, and incumbents are feasible.
Branching covers each parent region by its children.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On termination, the returned incumbent satisfies \(f(\hat x)-v^*\leq\varepsilon\).

children.title: Global LP-NLP Branching Search
children.top_down_role: Mixed-integer linear masters coordinated with globally bounded nonlinear subproblems.

children.title: LP Master Search
children.top_down_role: Mixed-integer linear master structures used to organize discrete search.

knowledge_statements.title: LP Master Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP relaxations drive branching and lower bounding inside a global LP–NLP search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node \(N\), form a linear master relaxation \(P_N\) containing variable bounds, linear constraints, integrality relaxations, and all globally valid or node-valid cuts applicable to \(N\). Solve \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}z:z\in P_N\}\). If \(P_N\) is infeasible, fathom \(N\); otherwise its optimum is the node lower bound \(L_N\). If \(L_N\geq U-\varepsilon\), fathom by bound. When the master solution violates integrality, branch on a fractional integer variable; when nonlinear relaxation error remains, branch spatially or request nonlinear separation. A candidate satisfying the master's discrete requirements is passed to the nonlinear subproblem stage. Stop when the active master queue is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The LP master supplies node lower bounds, detects linearized infeasibility, selects branching decisions, and sends discrete candidates to globally bounded nonlinear subproblems.
assumptions_latex: \(P_N\) contains the projection of every original feasible point in node \(N\).
Every inherited local cut is valid throughout node \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever \(P_N\neq\varnothing\), its optimum satisfies \(L_N\leq v(N)\).

notation.meaning: linear master relaxation at node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits LP Master Search, but the proposed LP–NLP protocol and branching behavior lack an architecture-specific source.

children.title: Global NLP Subproblem Bounding
children.top_down_role: Globally bounded nonlinear subproblems associated with master decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Global NLP Subproblem Bounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed-discrete nonlinear subproblem returns rigorous regional bounds or an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a master candidate integer vector \(y\) and spatial region \(B\), define the nonlinear subproblem value \(v(y,B)=\inf\{f(x,y):(x,y)\text{ is feasible},\ x\in B\}\). A global subproblem solver returns either a certified infeasibility result or numbers \(L(y,B)\) and \(U(y,B)\) with \(L(y,B)\leq v(y,B)\leq U(y,B)\), where a finite upper bound is supported by a feasible point. The lower certificate must derive from relaxations valid on all of \(B\), not merely from a local NLP optimum. If \(U(y,B)-L(y,B)\leq\eta\), the subproblem is globally solved to tolerance \(\eta\); otherwise its unresolved spatial regions remain eligible for refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global NLP subproblem certificate encloses the fixed-discrete regional optimum between a rigorous relaxation bound and a feasible-point value, or certifies infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The integer vector \(y\) is fixed and \(B\) is the certified spatial domain.
Lower estimators are valid throughout \(B\), and every reported upper bound comes from a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output certifies either infeasibility on \(\{y\}\times B\) or \(L(y,B)\leq v(y,B)\leq U(y,B)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind correctly reflects the terminal container, but the required global-NLP outputs and their role in this LP–NLP architecture need authoritative support.

children.title: Master–Subproblem Coordination
children.top_down_role: Information exchange between linear master search and nonlinear global bounding.

knowledge_statements.title: Master–Subproblem Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordination exchanges discrete candidates, rigorous nonlinear bounds, incumbents, and valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an LP master queue with the root relaxation and set \(U=+\infty\). Repeatedly select a master node, solve its LP relaxation, and discard it if infeasible or bounded by \(U\). Pass each admissible discrete candidate \(y\) and its spatial domain \(B\) to a global NLP subproblem. If the subproblem returns a feasible point, update \(U\); if it returns valid separating inequalities, add them globally or only to nodes contained in their validity domains; if its gap remains open, enqueue the required spatial children. Reoptimize affected master nodes. Terminate when every active master or nonlinear region has lower bound at least \(U-\varepsilon\), and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinator alternates master relaxations and global nonlinear subproblems, exchanging candidates, bounds, cuts, spatial children, and incumbent updates until the global gap closes.
assumptions_latex: All exchanged lower bounds and cuts retain their stated validity domains.
The queue processes every unresolved node fairly.
Every child collection covers its parent region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, every feasible solution has value at least \(U-\varepsilon\), so the incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the coordination container, but the combined queue, cut exchange, spatial-child, and termination protocol is uncited and architecture-specific.

children.title: Extended Cutting-Plane Globalization
children.top_down_role: Cutting-plane architectures augmented by global underestimation and spatial refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Cutting-Plane Globalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A cutting-plane master is globalized using valid underestimators and spatial refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start with a linear or mixed-integer master outer relaxation over the root domain. At each master solution \(\bar z\), evaluate nonlinear feasibility and separate violated constraints using affine or convex inequalities valid on the current domain. Cuts valid on the root domain enter the global pool; cuts valid only on a subregion are tagged locally. If no sufficiently strong valid cut is available because an estimator is loose, partition the responsible continuous interval and construct tighter estimators on the children. Feasible points update the incumbent \(U\), and relaxation optima provide lower bounds. Fathom infeasible or dominated regions, and stop when the smallest active lower bound is at least \(U-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extended cutting-plane search combines valid nonlinear cuts with spatial partitioning, tightening weak estimators until infeasibility, dominance, or the requested global gap is certified.
assumptions_latex: Every cut is valid on its recorded domain.
Spatial children cover their parent region without excluding feasible points.
Master optima are valid lower bounds and incumbents are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the algorithm stops, its incumbent \(\hat z\) satisfies \(f(\hat z)-v^*\leq\varepsilon\).

children.title: Nonconvex MINLP Cutting-Plane Tree Search
children.top_down_role: Integrated search combining nonlinear relaxations, mixed-integer cuts, and spatial branching.

children.title: Global Nonlinear-Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation of globally valid nonlinear estimators.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Nonlinear-Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A separated cut must be valid over the full declared domain and exclude the current relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a constraint \(g(z)\leq0\) on a declared domain \(D\), and let \(\bar z\in D\) be a master point. A function \(\ell\) is a global underestimator certificate when \(\ell(z)\leq g(z)\) for every \(z\in D\). The inequality \(\ell(z)\leq0\) is then valid for every point satisfying \(g(z)\leq0\). It separates \(\bar z\) when \(\ell(\bar z)>0\). Thus a verifiable separation certificate consists of the cut coefficients or formula, the domain \(D\), a justification of global underestimation on \(D\), and the positive violation at \(\bar z\). A locally valid underestimator is not a global-cut certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global nonlinear cut is certified by domain-wide underestimation and positive violation at the master point; merely local validity is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The original constraint is \(g(z)\leq0\) on \(D\).
The estimator satisfies \(\ell(z)\leq g(z)\) for all \(z\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(z)\leq0\) implies \(\ell(z)\leq0\) on \(D\), while \(\ell(\bar z)>0\) certifies separation of \(\bar z\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The underestimator implication and separation test are mathematically correct, and certificate is an appropriate kind, but this nontrivial global-cut certificate has no cited source.

children.title: Local Spatial-Cut Management
children.top_down_role: Management of cuts valid only within restricted spatial domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Spatial-Cut Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cuts valid only on restricted boxes are tagged, inherited selectively, and removed outside their domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent each local cut \(a^{\mathsf T}z\leq b\) together with a certified validity region \(D_c\). Attach it to a search node with domain \(D_N\) only when \(D_N\subseteq D_c\). When branching creates a child \(M\), inherit the cut exactly when \(D_M\subseteq D_c\); otherwise omit it or recompute a valid restriction. Never promote the cut to the global pool without a separate proof of validity on the root domain. Cuts may be deleted for efficiency, since deletion only weakens the relaxation, but applying a cut outside \(D_c\) can remove feasible solutions and invalidate global bounds. Store domain tags with cut-pool and node-reoptimization records.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local cuts carry explicit validity regions, pass only to contained descendants, and may be dropped safely; using them outside their regions can destroy correctness.
assumptions_latex: Each local cut has a certified validity region \(D_c\).
Every node has a known domain \(D_N\), and containment can be verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If cuts are applied only when \(D_N\subseteq D_c\), no feasible point in a processed node is excluded by an out-of-domain local cut.

notation.meaning: certified validity region of a local cut

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits local spatial-cut management, but inheritance, deletion, promotion, and domain-tagging policies require an inspectable source.

children.title: Integrality-Cut Integration
children.top_down_role: Coordination between nonlinear relaxation cuts and mixed-integer cut families.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Cut Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-aware coordination of nonlinear-relaxation and mixed-integer cuts within spatial branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set of a minimization MINLP and let \(F_B:=F\cap B\) be its feasible set in node domain \(B\). Construct a mixed-integer relaxation \(R_B\supseteq F_B\) using valid nonlinear-relaxation inequalities and mixed-integer cuts, and let \(L_B\) be its optimal value. Install a cut globally only when it is valid on the root domain; a cut valid only on \(B\) may be used only at \(B\) and descendants whose domains are contained in \(B\). If a relaxation solution violates integrality, branch or separate a valid mixed-integer cut. If it satisfies integrality but violates an original nonlinear relation, separate a valid nonlinear cut or globally solve the corresponding fixed-integer nonlinear subproblem. Prune when \(R_B=\varnothing\) or \(L_B\ge U-\varepsilon\), where \(U\) is a feasible incumbent value and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each node, combine valid integer and nonlinear cuts, respect every cut's validity domain, evaluate integral candidates globally when necessary, and prune only with certified infeasibility or lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) contains every feasible point assigned to the node and each descendant domain is contained in its parent domain.
Every installed inequality is valid on its declared global or local domain.
\(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With \(f_B^*:=\inf\{f(x):x\in F_B\}\), the relaxation bound satisfies \(L_B\le f_B^*\); hence the stated infeasibility and bound-based pruning tests are valid.

notation.meaning: exact feasible set in node domain B
infimum of the original objective over the node-feasible set

children.title: Nested Global-Optimization Architectures

children.title: Global NLP inside Integer Search
children.top_down_role: Integer search using continuous global optimization for node or assignment evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Global NLP inside Integer Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer search using deterministic global nonlinear optimization for node bounds and fixed-assignment evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the minimization MINLP \(\min\{f(x,y):(x,y)\in F,\ y\in Y\cap\mathbb Z^p\}\). Maintain nodes \(D\subseteq Y\cap\mathbb Z^p\). At each node obtain a certified lower bound \(L_D\) by globally solving a valid continuous relaxation of the problem restricted to \(y\in D\). When \(D=\{\widehat y\}\), globally solve the fixed-integer NLP, certifying infeasibility or obtaining its global optimum and feasible solutions. Update the incumbent \(U\) from feasible solutions and prune if the node is certified infeasible or \(L_D\ge U-\varepsilon\). Otherwise partition \(D\) into finitely many children whose union contains every integer assignment in \(D\). Stop when no active node has lower bound below \(U-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search over integer domains, use globally solved continuous relaxations for node bounds, and globally solve the nonlinear problem when an integer assignment is fixed.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\cap\mathbb Z^p\) is finite, or the integer search is otherwise finitely exhaustive.
Every continuous node relaxation supplies a valid global lower bound for its restricted integer node.
Every fixed-integer NLP is solved globally or certified infeasible.
Every branching partition preserves all integer assignments, and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the MINLP is feasible, termination returns a feasible incumbent with value at most \(f^*+\varepsilon\), where \(f^*\) is the global MINLP optimum; if every node is certified infeasible, the method certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: current set of admissible integer assignments
fixed integer assignment at a singleton node
certified lower bound for node D

children.title: MILP Master inside Spatial Search
children.top_down_role: Spatial search using mixed-integer linear master relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: MILP Master inside Spatial Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial branch-and-bound driven by mixed-integer linear outer relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization MINLP and node domain \(B\), replace every nonconvex factor relation by linear inequalities valid on \(B\), retain the applicable integrality restrictions, and solve the resulting MILP master to obtain its value \(L_B\). If the master solution violates a represented nonlinear relation, add a valid estimator cut. Otherwise use it to seek or verify a feasible incumbent. When a material relaxation error remains, split an integer domain or continuous interval so that the children cover the parent domain, and rebuild local estimators on the child boxes. Prune an infeasible master or a node satisfying \(L_B\ge U-\varepsilon\). Terminate only when no active node has lower bound below \(U-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A MILP master supplies valid node bounds while spatial branching and local estimator refinement reduce nonlinear relaxation gaps.
assumptions_latex: Every master inequality outer-approximates the feasible set or underestimates the objective on \(B\).
Branching children cover every feasible point of their parent node.
Estimator gaps converge to zero under exhaustive box refinement.
\(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f_B^*\) denotes the original node optimum, then \(L_B\le f_B^*\). If the method terminates by the stated active-node gap test, its incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal.

notation.meaning: MILP master value at node B
optimal value of the original MINLP restricted to node B

children.title: GOP-Based MINLP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces between primal–relaxed-dual decomposition and mixed-integer global search.

knowledge_statements.title: GOP-Based MINLP Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-preserving interface between GOP subproblems and mixed-integer search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a mixed-integer search node \(D\), a GOP interface passes fixed or restricted integer variables to a primal problem and returns feasible primal values as upper bounds. Its relaxed-dual construction returns a value \(L_D\) no larger than the infimum of the original node problem; when reformulated as a MILP, all binary variables and linearized relaxed-dual constraints must preserve that bound. The integer-search layer may prune \(D\) only after certified infeasibility or when \(L_D\ge U-\varepsilon\), and any branching disjunction must cover every assignment in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface exchanges GOP primal incumbents and relaxed-dual lower bounds without weakening the validity requirements of integer search.
assumptions_latex: The node model has the separability and regularity required by the selected GOP formulation.
The relaxed-dual or MILP reformulation supplies a certified global lower bound.
\(U\) is obtained from a feasible MINLP point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: GOP bounds can be used safely for mixed-integer pruning, and exhaustion of the search establishes \(\varepsilon\)-global optimality.

children.title: AlphaBB-Based MINLP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Mixed-integer search using curvature-corrected continuous lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: AlphaBB-Based MINLP Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boxwise convex underestimators used as lower-bounding representations within mixed-integer search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:B\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable on the box \(B=[l,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\). Define \[h_{\alpha}(x)=h(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(l_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i),\qquad \alpha_i\ge0.\] Because \((l_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\le0\) on \(B\), one has \(h_{\alpha}(x)\le h(x)\). Choose \(\alpha\) so that \(h_{\alpha}\) is convex on \(B\). For a minimization problem with objective \(f\) and constraints \(g_j(x)\le0\), replacing \(f\) and each \(g_j\) by such convex underestimators produces an outer lower-bounding formulation. With integer variables fixed it is a continuous convex relaxation; with unfixed integer variables retained it is a mixed-integer convex relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AlphaBB adds box-dependent quadratic corrections that convexify objective and less-than-or-equal constraint functions while underestimating them, yielding valid continuous or mixed-integer lower-bounding formulations.
assumptions_latex: \(B=[l,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\) is compact.
Each corrected function is twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(B\).
Each chosen correction vector is nonnegative and makes its corrected function convex on \(B\).
Every relaxed nonlinear constraint is written in the form \(g_j(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L_B\) is the relaxation optimum and \(f_B^*\) is the original node optimum, then \(L_B\le f_B^*\), so \(L_B\) is valid for mixed-integer pruning.

notation.meaning: alphaBB convex underestimator of a function h
optimal value of the original node problem

children.title: Couenne Symbolic Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Expression decomposition and auxiliary-variable representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Couenne Symbolic Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-variable decomposition of nonlinear expression graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a factorable MINLP, assign an auxiliary variable \(w_v\) to each selected internal node \(v\) of its expression directed acyclic graph. If node \(v\) represents the atomic operation \(\phi_v\) applied to predecessors \(p(v)\), impose \(w_v=\phi_v(w_{p(v)})\), and replace every occurrence of the original subexpression by \(w_v\). Preserve original variable bounds and integrality declarations. Projection of the resulting extended formulation onto the original variables equals the original feasible set, while relaxing each atomic equality separately permits localized envelopes, propagation, and spatial branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Couenne decomposes factorable expressions into auxiliary variables and atomic equalities whose projection reproduces the original model.
assumptions_latex: Every nonlinear expression is factorable into supported atomic operations.
Auxiliary equalities are imposed exactly before relaxation.
Domains exclude undefined atomic operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact extended formulation is projection-equivalent to the original MINLP and exposes atomic relations for global relaxation.

notation.meaning: auxiliary variable for expression node v

review_flags: Couenne-specific symbolic-reformulation documentation and exact locator required

children.title: Couenne Relaxation-Cut System

children.title: Couenne Relaxation Construction
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral relaxation structures generated from reformulated nonlinear expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Couenne Relaxation Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nodewise convex relaxation of Couenne’s auxiliary-variable formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each atomic relation \(w_v=\phi_v(z_v)\) and current node box \(B\), replace equality by a convex set \(R_{v,B}\) containing its graph over \(B\). Retain linear constraints and integrality declarations, and replace a nonlinear objective by an auxiliary epigraph variable with a valid convex underestimator. The intersection \(R_B=\bigcap_v R_{v,B}\) is then an outer relaxation of the reformulated feasible set on \(B\). Minimizing the relaxed objective over \(R_B\) supplies a valid lower bound; tighter envelopes may be reconstructed after bound reduction or branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Couenne builds a node relaxation by replacing each atomic expression relation with a valid convex graph enclosure over current bounds.
assumptions_latex: All atomic-variable bounds on \(B\) are valid.
Each \(R_{v,B}\) contains the corresponding graph on \(B\).
The relaxed objective globally underestimates the original objective on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation satisfies \(F_B\subseteq R_B\), and its optimum is no greater than the node’s true optimum.

notation.meaning: relaxation of atomic relation v on box B
exact reformulated feasible set on B

review_flags: Couenne relaxation-construction documentation and exact locator required

children.title: Couenne Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Detection of violated nonlinear estimators within Couenne search.

knowledge_statements.title: Couenne Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of violated valid estimators at a relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At node box \(B
eq\varnothing\), solve the current relaxation and obtain \(\bar z\). For each atomic relation, invoke an applicable estimator oracle to produce an inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}z\le b\) valid for its graph on \(B\). Add the inequality when \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar z>b+\tau\), where \(\tau\ge0\) is the separation tolerance; record it as global only when validity holds on the root domain, and otherwise attach it locally to \(B\). Reoptimize and repeat until no eligible violation exceeds \(\tau\), a resource limit is reached, or branching is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Couenne detects violated atomic estimators, adds them with the correct validity domain, and reoptimizes until separation stops.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation solution \(\bar z\) is available.
Every estimator oracle returns an inequality valid on its declared domain.
\(\tau\ge0\) is fixed for the separation round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted cut preserves all feasible points in its validity domain and excludes the current point whenever its violation exceeds \(\tau\).

children.title: Couenne Cut-Pool Management
children.top_down_role: Retention, activation, and retirement regimes for generated cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Couenne Cut-Pool Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-aware storage, activation, and retirement of relaxation cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Store each generated cut \(c	o a_c^{\mathsf T}z\le b_c\) together with its validity domain \(V_c\), origin, age, efficacy, and activity status. At node box \(B\\), a cut is eligible only if \(B\subseteq V_c\). Activate eligible cuts whose violation or predicted bound improvement exceeds prescribed tolerances; merge duplicates and numerically equivalent cuts. A cut may be deactivated after sustained inactivity, but deletion or reuse must never erase its domain restriction. Globally valid cuts may be shared throughout the tree, whereas locally valid cuts may pass only to descendants contained in \(V_c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cut pool tracks validity and usefulness so global cuts are shared safely while local cuts remain confined to compatible descendants.
assumptions_latex: Every stored cut has a certified validity domain \(V_c\).
Node domains are nested along descendant paths.
Cut comparison and activity tests use fixed numerical tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any cut activated at node \(B\) is valid for every feasible point in \(B\), so pool management cannot invalidate the node relaxation.
review_flags: Couenne cut-pool policy and exact software documentation required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits cut-pool management, but the detailed storage, efficacy, duplicate-merging, aging, and inheritance policy is unsupported. The fragment defining the node box also contains a malformed extra LaTeX line-break command.

children.title: Couenne Bound-Reduction System
children.top_down_role: Feasibility- and optimization-driven domain reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Couenne Bound-Reduction System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility- and optimization-based tightening of node variable domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given node box \(B=[l,u]\), first propagate every atomic relation and linear constraint to a fixed point, intersecting inferred intervals with \(B\); prune if any interval becomes empty. For optimization-based tightening, minimize and maximize selected variable \(x_i\) over a valid relaxation augmented by the incumbent cutoff, then replace \(l_i\) and \(u_i\) by certified rounded bounds derived from those optima. Rebuild affected envelopes after material tightening. Every update must retain all feasible points whose objective is below the incumbent cutoff; iteration stops at a fixed point or a resource limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Couenne combines interval propagation and relaxation-based subproblems to tighten bounds without removing any potentially improving feasible point.
assumptions_latex: Initial bounds contain every feasible point of the node.
Propagation operators and optimization relaxations are valid outer approximations.
The incumbent cutoff is imposed only from a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced box \(B'\subseteq B\) contains every node-feasible point capable of improving the incumbent; \(B'=\varnothing\) certifies node infeasibility.
review_flags: Couenne bound-reduction documentation and exact locator required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits bound reduction, but the propagation and optimization-based tightening workflow lacks Couenne documentation. Moreover, emptiness after applying an incumbent cutoff certifies absence of an improving feasible point, not necessarily infeasibility of the original node.

children.title: Couenne Spatial Branching System
children.top_down_role: Coordination of integrality and nonlinear spatial branching.

knowledge_statements.title: Couenne Spatial Branching System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint branching on fractional integer variables and nonlinear relaxation errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an unpruned node \(B\), score eligible integer variables using fractionality and eligible continuous or auxiliary variables using nonlinear relaxation violation, estimated bound gain, or domain width. Select one candidate. For integer \(y_j\) at relaxation value \(\bar y_j\notin\mathbb Z\), create children \(y_j\le\lfloor\bar y_j\rfloor\) and \(y_j\ge\lceil\bar y_j\rceil\). For continuous \(x_i\) and split point \(s\in(l_i,u_i)\), create children \(x_i\in[l_i,s]\) and \(x_i\in[s,u_i]\). Rebuild local relaxations and propagate bounds in every child.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Couenne selects between integrality and spatial disjunctions, creates exhaustive children, and reconstructs tighter local relaxations.
assumptions_latex: The selected split point lies strictly inside the current continuous interval.
Each branching disjunction covers the parent domain.
Child bounds are propagated without excluding feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The union of the children contains every feasible point of \(B\), while the selected integrality or spatial ambiguity is reduced.

notation.meaning: fractional relaxation value of integer variable j

review_flags: Couenne branching-score and coordination documentation required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exhaustive branching disjunctions are mathematically sound and the algorithm kind fits, but the Couenne-specific scoring criteria and coordination between integrality and spatial candidates require an inspectable software or scholarly source.

children.title: SCIP Nonlinear Structure Detection
children.top_down_role: Recognition of specialized nonlinear structures by expression handlers.

knowledge_statements.title: SCIP Nonlinear Structure Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expression-handler recognition of exploitable nonlinear substructures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Traverse each nonlinear expression directed acyclic graph bottom-up. At expression node \(v\), query registered handlers for a representation \(r_v\) and a validity domain \(D_v\) that match the operator, curvature, monotonicity, bounds, and child representations. Accept a detection only when its recognition predicate is satisfied on \(D_v\); handlers may then register domain propagation, feasibility checking, convex or concave estimators, and branching candidates. If several detections overlap, retain only a compatible handler assignment. Unrecognized nodes remain represented by the generic expression system, so detection changes available inference mechanisms but not the exact modeled expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SCIP handlers recognize nonlinear subexpressions and attach valid propagation, estimation, checking, and branching methods without changing the modeled function.
assumptions_latex: The expression graph is finite and its variable bounds are valid.
Each handler states a checkable recognition predicate and validity domain.
Accepted handler representations agree with the original expression on their domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every registered inference method is valid on its declared domain, while fallback handling preserves the original nonlinear expression semantics.

notation.meaning: detected structural representation at node v
domain on which the detection is valid

review_flags: SCIP expression-handler documentation and version-specific locator required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches structure detection, but expression-handler recognition, compatibility selection, registered callbacks, and fallback semantics are SCIP-version-specific claims without documentation or a versioned locator.

children.title: SCIP Estimation-Separation System
children.top_down_role: Generation and separation of nonlinear estimators.

children.title: SCIP Expression Estimation
children.top_down_role: Construction of nonlinear estimators from detected expression structure.

knowledge_statements.title: SCIP Expression Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local under- and overestimation of a nonlinear expression on a bounded node domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:D\to\mathbb R\) be a nonlinear expression on a box \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). An expression estimator at reference point \(\bar x\in D\) is an affine function \(a(x)=\alpha^{\mathsf T}x+\beta\). It is an underestimator when \(a(x)\le h(x)\) for every \(x\in D\), and an overestimator when \(a(x)\ge h(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Replacing \(w=h(x)\) by \(w\ge a(x)\) or \(w\le a(x)\), respectively, yields a relaxation valid on \(D\); equality at \(\bar x\) makes the estimator locally tight there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SCIP may replace a nonlinear expression by an affine lower or upper bound that is valid throughout the current node domain and optionally tight at a reference point.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty bounded box.
\(h(x)\) is finite on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w=h(x)\Rightarrow w\ge a(x)\) for an underestimator, and \(w=h(x)\Rightarrow w\le a(x)\) for an overestimator, on \(D\).
review_flags: SCIP-specific estimator interface and conventions require an authoritative SCIP locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic estimator statement is mathematically coherent and the representation kind fits, but no inspectable SCIP source supports the SCIP-specific terminology and conventions.

children.title: SCIP Nonlinear Separation
children.top_down_role: Identification of violated estimators during global search.

knowledge_statements.title: SCIP Nonlinear Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of violated estimator inequalities from a nonlinear relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation solution \((\hat x,\hat w)\) and a bounded domain \(D\), select an expression \(w=h(x)\) whose current relaxation is violated or insufficiently tight. Construct a valid affine underestimator \(a^-\) or overestimator \(a^+\) on \(D\). Add \(w\ge a^-(x)\) when \(\hat w<a^-(\hat x)-\varepsilon\), or add \(w\le a^+(x)\) when \(\hat w>a^+(\hat x)+\varepsilon\). Reoptimize and repeat until no candidate inequality has violation exceeding \(\varepsilon\), or a prescribed separation limit is reached; return the strengthened relaxation and its solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a relaxation solution, generate domain-valid estimator cuts violated beyond tolerance, add them, and reoptimize until no qualifying cut or a limit remains.
assumptions_latex: \((\hat x,\hat w)\) solves the current relaxation.
\(a^-\le h\le a^+\) holds throughout \(D\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\) is the separation tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every added inequality is valid for all points satisfying \(w=h(x)\) with \(x\in D\).
review_flags: SCIP-specific separation scheduling and acceptance rules require an authoritative SCIP locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm describes plausible estimator-cut separation, but its selection, tolerance, repetition, and stopping rules require an authoritative SCIP locator.

children.title: Estimator Validity Domains
children.top_down_role: Local or global domains over which SCIP estimators remain valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Estimator Validity Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate ensuring that a nonlinear estimator remains valid after domain changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h:D\to\mathbb R\) and \(E\subseteq D\), an affine function \(a\) is a valid underestimator on \(E\) exactly when \(a(x)\le h(x)\) for every \(x\in E\); it is a valid overestimator exactly when \(a(x)\ge h(x)\) for every \(x\in E\). Consequently, validity on \(D\) implies validity on every restricted domain \(E\subseteq D\). After expansion to \(E\not\subseteq D\), the old estimator is reusable only if its defining inequality is independently verified throughout \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimator validity is universal over its declared domain; restriction preserves validity, whereas domain expansion requires a new verification.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(a\) are finite on the domain being tested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\subseteq D\) and \(a\le h\) on \(D\) imply \(a\le h\) on \(E\), with the analogous implication for overestimators.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: universal inequalities are preserved under restriction of their domain.

children.title: SCIP Expression Domain Propagation
children.top_down_role: Handler-mediated propagation through nonlinear expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: SCIP Expression Domain Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward and reverse interval propagation through a nonlinear expression graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an acyclic expression graph, initialize each variable node with its current interval \(X_i\). In a forward pass, assign every operator node \(v=\phi(u_1,\ldots,u_k)\) an interval enclosure \(V\supseteq\{\phi(z):z_j\in U_j\}\). Intersect the root interval with the constraint-permitted range. In a reverse pass, each expression handler computes sound child enclosures \(U'_j\) satisfying every feasible tuple consistent with the tightened parent range, and updates \(U_j\leftarrow U_j\cap U'_j\). Iterate until no interval changes beyond tolerance; report infeasibility if any interval becomes empty, otherwise return the contracted intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate intervals forward through expression operators and backward from constraint ranges, repeatedly intersecting domains until stable or an empty interval proves infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Each operator handler supplies inclusion-monotone forward enclosures.
Each reverse-propagation rule preserves every feasible child value.
The expression graph is acyclic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned intervals contain every feasible value admitted by the input intervals and nonlinear constraints.

notation.meaning: operator represented by an expression node

review_flags: SCIP expression-handler propagation semantics require an authoritative SCIP locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is a sound generic propagation scheme, but the exact SCIP expression-handler workflow and iteration semantics are not supported by an inspectable source.

children.title: SCIP Spatial Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching on variables participating in unresolved nonconvex structure.

knowledge_statements.title: SCIP Spatial Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain partitioning on variables responsible for unresolved nonconvex relaxation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with box \(D=\prod_i[\ell_i,u_i]\), compute branching scores for variables occurring in nonconvex expressions, using relaxation violation, estimator error, or domain width. Choose \(j\) with positive score and a split point \(s\in(\ell_j,u_j)\). Create child domains \(D^- = D\cap\{x:x_j\le s\}\) and \(D^+ = D\cap\{x:x_j\ge s\}\), then recompute propagation and estimators on each child. Fathom a child when infeasibility is detected or its valid lower bound cannot improve the incumbent; otherwise retain it for search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a variable contributing to nonconvex relaxation error, split its interval, rebuild child relaxations, and prune children by infeasibility or bound dominance.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the current bounded node box.
Each child relaxation supplies a valid lower bound for minimization.
A finite incumbent value is used when available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=D^-\cup D^+\), so branching preserves every feasible point while permitting tighter child relaxations.

source_refs.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

children.title: BARON Branch–Reduce–Bound Architecture

knowledge_statements.title: BARON Branch–Reduce–Bound Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract branch–reduce–bound workflow associated with BARON, excluding undocumented implementation choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a list with the original bounded MINLP domain and an incumbent upper bound \(U=+\infty\). For a selected node domain \(D\), apply feasibility-based and optimality-based range reduction, construct a convex relaxation, and obtain a valid lower bound \(L(D)\). Use a feasible local solution to update \(U\). Discard \(D\) if it is infeasible or \(L(D)\ge U-\varepsilon\); otherwise partition \(D\) and insert its children. Stop when the list is empty or \(U-\min_D L(D)\le\varepsilon\), returning the incumbent and the bound gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BARON’s abstract architecture alternates domain reduction, relaxation bounds, incumbent improvement, pruning, and branching until the global bound gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The original variable domain is bounded.
Every node relaxation gives a valid minimization lower bound.
Every incumbent is feasible for the original MINLP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination by the gap test, the incumbent objective is within \(\varepsilon\) of the global optimum.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound on node domain

source_refs.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

children.title: ANTIGONE Algebraic Branching Search Architecture
children.top_down_role: ANTIGONE as a representative algebraic reformulation and spatial-search architecture.

children.title: ANTIGONE Algebraic Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Algebraic transformations used to expose globally searchable nonlinear structure.

knowledge_statements.title: ANTIGONE Algebraic Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorable reformulation into elementary relations suitable for convex relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a factorable nonlinear model contain a composite expression \(f(x)\). Introduce one auxiliary variable for each nontrivial subexpression, obtaining equations \(w_k=\phi_k(z_k)\) whose arguments are original or earlier auxiliary variables, and replace occurrences of \(f(x)\) by its root variable. The reformulation is exact under projection when auxiliary equations are imposed: \(x\) is feasible for the original model if and only if there exists \(w\) satisfying the reformulated model, and corresponding objective values agree. Replacing selected equations by valid convex relaxations yields a lower-bounding relaxation for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decompose composite factorable expressions into auxiliary elementary equations; exact equations preserve the model under projection, while convex relaxations provide global lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: Every nonlinear expression has a finite factorable expression graph on the working box.
Auxiliary equations follow an acyclic dependency order.
Relaxations are valid on the declared variable domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_{\mathrm{reform}})=F_{\mathrm{original}}\), and relaxing auxiliary equations produces a superset of \(F_{\mathrm{reform}}\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the exact reformulation

review_flags: ANTIGONE-specific reformulation rules and supported operator classes require primary documentation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is a standard factorable reformulation, but its attribution to ANTIGONE and the implied supported reformulation rules require primary documentation.

children.title: ANTIGONE Spatial Search
children.top_down_role: Spatial partitioning and bounding within the ANTIGONE architecture.

knowledge_statements.title: ANTIGONE Spatial Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial branch-and-bound applied to algebraically reformulated nonconvex relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start from the bounded domain of an algebraically reformulated MINLP. At each active node \(D\), propagate bounds, solve a convex relaxation to obtain \(L(D)\), and attempt to obtain a feasible incumbent \(U\). If \(D\) is not pruned by infeasibility or \(L(D)\ge U-\varepsilon\), select a variable appearing in a relaxed nonconvex relation and partition its interval into child domains. Rebuild domain-dependent relaxations on the children. Continue until no active node remains or the incumbent-to-global-lower-bound gap is at most \(\varepsilon\); return the incumbent and certified gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search the reformulated model by repeatedly bounding, pruning, and splitting domains of variables occurring in unresolved nonconvex relations.
assumptions_latex: All active node domains are bounded.
Node relaxations provide valid lower bounds.
Branching partitions each selected node domain without losing feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(U-\min_D L(D)\le\varepsilon\), the returned incumbent is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.6 Branch-and-Bound Strategies p. 33

review_flags: Generic spatial branch-and-bound is supported provisionally; ANTIGONE-specific search rules need primary documentation.

children.title: Reformulation–Search Coupling
children.top_down_role: Architectural dependence of spatial search on the selected algebraic representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Reformulation–Search Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node domains control relaxation strength for reformulated elementary relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an exact factorable reformulation with auxiliary relations \(w_k=\phi_k(z_k)\) and a spatial-search node domain \(D\). Each node relaxation must be constructed using estimators valid on \(D\). If branching replaces \(D\) by subsets \(D_1,D_2\), estimators may be recomputed on each child; their relaxation feasible sets \(R(D_i)\) must contain the exact reformulated feasible points in \(D_i\). When the chosen envelopes converge to the corresponding expression graphs as relevant interval diameters vanish, exhaustive nested partitioning drives the local relaxation error to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Algebraic reformulation exposes elementary relations, while spatial branching shrinks their domains so valid envelopes can be recomputed and progressively tightened.
assumptions_latex: The reformulation is exact under projection.
Every node estimator is valid on its node domain.
Elementary envelopes converge as their argument intervals shrink.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap D_i\subseteq R(D_i)\), and along nested domains of vanishing relevant diameter the associated envelope error tends to \(0\).
review_flags: A source is needed for the precise envelope-convergence conditions used by ANTIGONE.

children.title: Solver Architecture Comparison Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on comparing named solvers as interchangeable implementations.

children.title: Proprietary-Mechanism Visibility
children.top_down_role: Comparison limits caused by undocumented solver mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Proprietary-Mechanism Visibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit on architectural claims when solver mechanisms are not publicly documented.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O_{S,I}\) denote the observable output of solver \(S\) on instance \(I\), and let \(M_1\neq M_2\) be internal mechanisms that both produce \(O_{S,I}\) for every tested instance \(I\in\mathcal T\). Then observations on \(\mathcal T\) do not identify which mechanism is implemented. Consequently, benchmark logs can support claims about measured outcomes—such as runtime, returned objective, or reported bound—but cannot by themselves certify undocumented branching scores, reformulations, cut-generation rules, or scheduling policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical observed solver behavior can arise from different hidden mechanisms, so benchmarks alone cannot establish undocumented internal architecture.
assumptions_latex: Only input-output behavior and public logs are observable.
At least two distinct internal mechanisms are observationally equivalent on the test set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_1\neq M_2\) and \(O_{M_1,I}=O_{M_2,I}\) for all \(I\in\mathcal T\) imply that the implemented mechanism is not identifiable from \(\mathcal T\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: observational equivalence prevents identification of an unobserved mechanism.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Version-Dependent Solver Architectures
children.top_down_role: Architectural changes across solver versions.

knowledge_statements.title: Version-Dependent Solver Architectures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver architecture claims are indexed by release and configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a solver architecture by \(A(v,c)\), where \(v\) is the solver version and \(c\) is its build and parameter configuration. An architectural statement established for \((v_0,c_0)\) transfers to \((v_1,c_1)\) only when the claimed component is documented or verified to be invariant between those pairs. If branching, presolve, relaxation, propagation, or separation changes, equality \(A(v_0,c_0)=A(v_1,c_1)\) cannot be inferred from the shared solver name. Reproducible comparisons must therefore report \((v,c)\) and restrict conclusions to the tested or documented configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver name does not guarantee architectural invariance across releases; comparisons must identify versions and configurations and limit claims accordingly.
assumptions_latex: Solver behavior may depend on version, build, and parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absent an invariance record, a claim about \(A(v_0,c_0)\) does not entail the same claim about \(A(v_1,c_1)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: software behavior and components are configuration-indexed and need not persist across releases.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Modeling-System Reformulation Effects
children.top_down_role: Structural transformations applied before a solver receives a model.

knowledge_statements.title: Modeling-System Reformulation Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pre-solver transformations can change the representation on which solver mechanisms operate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a modeling system transform an original model \(P\) into \(T(P)\) before solver invocation. If the transformation is exact, feasible solutions and objective values satisfy \(F_P=\operatorname{proj}_x(F_{T(P)})\); nevertheless, auxiliary variables, expression graphs, constraint counts, sparsity, and visible convexity may differ. Because propagation, estimator construction, branching candidates, and relaxations operate on the received representation, two exact transformations \(T_1(P)\) and \(T_2(P)\) can induce different search trajectories and computational outcomes while representing the same optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact preprocessing can preserve feasible solutions and objectives while changing the expression structure seen by the solver, thereby changing its search behavior.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is exact under projection onto the original variables.
The solver operates on the transformed representation rather than the unreformed source model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact equivalence of \(P\) and \(T(P)\) does not imply equality of their solver search trees, relaxations, or runtimes.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: extended formulations can be projection-equivalent while presenting different algebraic structures to algorithms.

children.title: Valid MINLP Bound Families
